title.zh: 卷四十八 列傳第十八 向雄 段灼 閻纘
title.en: Volume 48 Biographies 18: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan
title.raw: 卷四十八 列傳第十八 向雄 段灼 閻纘 Volume 48 Biographies 18: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan

sentences.zh: 向雄 段灼 閻纘

translations.literal: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong; Duan Zhuo; Yan Zuan

sentences.zh: 向雄，字茂伯，河內山陽人也。

translations.literal: Xiang Xiong, style name Maobo, was a man of Shanyang in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong, courtesy name Maobo, came from Shanyang in Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父韶，彭城太守。

translations.literal: His father Shao was prefect of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Xiang Shao, was prefect of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 雄初仕郡為主簿，事太守王經。

translations.literal: Xiong first served the commandery as chief clerk, attending prefect Wang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He began as the commandery chief clerk under Prefect Wang Jing.

sentences.zh: 及經之死也，雄哭之盡哀，市人咸為之悲。

translations.literal: When Jing died, Xiong wept for him to the utmost; market-goers all were moved for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jing was executed, Xiang Xiong mourned him without restraint, and the crowd in the market wept with him.

sentences.zh: 後太守劉毅嘗以非罪笞雄，及吳奮代毅為太守，又以少譴系雄於獄。

translations.literal: Later prefect Liu Yi once flogged Xiong without real crime, and when Wu Fen replaced Yi as prefect, again for a slight fault bound Xiong in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prefect Liu Yi had him flogged on a trumped-up charge; when Wu Fen succeeded Liu, he jailed Xiang Xiong again over a petty fault.

sentences.zh: 司隸鐘會於獄中辟雄為都官從事，會死無人殯斂，雄迎喪而葬之。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Area Commander Zhong Hui in prison recruited Xiong as adjutant for capital offices; when Hui died none arranged the funeral—Xiong received the corpse and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Director Zhong Hui recruited him from prison as an adjutant; when Zhong Hui died with no one to lay him out, Xiang Xiong claimed the body and gave him burial.

sentences.zh: 文帝召雄而責之曰：「往者王經之死，卿哭王經於東市，我不問也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen summoned Xiong and rebuked him: "In the past when Wang Jing died, you wept for Wang Jing at the eastern market—I did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen summoned him and scolded him: "When Wang Jing died you wailed for him at the Eastern Market—I let that pass."

sentences.zh: 今鐘會躬為叛逆，又輒收葬，若復相容，其如王法何！

translations.literal: Now Zhong Hui himself was traitorous, yet you again took in and buried him—if we again tolerate this, what of the king's law!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui was a declared traitor, yet you buried him too. If the law indulges that, what becomes of the statute?"

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「昔者先王掩骼埋胔，仁流朽骨，當時豈先卜其功罪而後葬之哉！

translations.literal: " Xiong said: "Ancient kings covered bones and buried flesh scraps; kindness flowed to withered bones—did they first weigh merit and crime then bury them!
translations.idiomatic: " Xiang Xiong replied: "The kings of old gathered exposed bones and buried the dead; their kindness reached dry bones—did they first judge guilt and merit before they buried anyone?"

sentences.zh: 今王誅既加，於法已備。

translations.literal: Now the royal punishment is already applied; in law it is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Royal punishment has already been inflicted; the law has run its course."

sentences.zh: 雄感義收葬，教亦無闕。

translations.literal: I, moved by righteousness, took and buried him—there is also no lack in instruction.
translations.idiomatic: I buried him out of decency toward a fallen man; that offends no moral teaching I know of."

sentences.zh: 法立於上，教弘於下，何必使雄違生背死以立于時！

translations.literal: Law is set above, instruction spreads below—why must I betray the living and turn my back on the dead to stand in the age!
translations.idiomatic: Statute comes from the throne and custom from the people—must I betray the living and insult the dead just to please the fashion?"

sentences.zh: 殿下仇枯骨而捐之中野，為將來仁賢之資，不亦惜乎！

translations.literal: Would Your Highness make sport of dry bones and cast them in the wilds, to be a fund for later worthies—is it not a pity!"
translations.idiomatic: Would you leave bleached bones in the ditch as a lesson to future good men—would that not be the greater shame?"

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅，與談宴而遣之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was much pleased, talked and feasted with him, then sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased, talked with him over wine, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 累遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted to gentleman of the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 時吳奮、劉毅俱為侍中，同在門下，雄初不交言。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Fen and Liu Yi were both palace attendants, together in the gate bureau, and at first Xiong spoke not a word with them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fen and Liu Yi were both palace attendants in the same bureau, and Xiang Xiong refused to speak with either.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞之，敕雄令復君臣之好。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard of it and ordered Xiong to restore cordial relations between superior and subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu heard of it, he ordered Xiang Xiong to mend fences with Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 雄不得已，乃詣毅，再拜曰：「向被詔命，君臣義絕，如何？

translations.literal: Xiong had no choice; he went to Yi and twice bowed: "We have just received an edict—duty between superior and subordinate is severed—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: He went to Liu Yi, bowed twice, and said, "The edict has just cut off all duty between superior and subordinate—what is left to say?"

sentences.zh: 」於是即去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he left at once.
translations.idiomatic: With that he turned and left.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而大怒，問雄曰：「我令卿復君臣之好，何以故絕？

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was greatly angry, asked Xiong: "I ordered you to restore cordial relations between superior and subordinate—why do you sever them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demanded, "I told you to make peace with Liu Yi—why did you break it off?"

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「古之君子進人以禮，退人以禮；

translations.literal: " Xiong said: "Ancient gentlemen advanced others with ritual and sent them away with ritual;
translations.idiomatic: " Xiang Xiong said, "The gentlemen of old advanced men with courtesy and dismissed them with courtesy;

sentences.zh: 今之進人若加諸膝，退人若墜諸川。

translations.literal: today's advancing others is like placing them on one's knee; sending them away is like dropping them into a gully.
translations.idiomatic: today people lift a favorite onto their knees and drop a fallen man into the pit."

sentences.zh: 劉河內於臣不為戎首，亦已幸甚，安復為君臣之好！

translations.literal: Liu of Henei toward your subject did not act as a war-leader—that is already very fortunate; how again restore cordial relations between superior and subordinate!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi of Henei did not strike the first blow against me—that is mercy enough; how can you call us cordial lord and minister again?"

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，累遷秦州刺史，假赤幢、曲蓋、鼓吹，賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: In Taishi era by stages he was promoted inspector of Qin province, given vermilion canopy, curved carriage awning, and martial music, granted two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era he rose to inspector of Qin province with crimson banner, curved awning, military band, and a grant of two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，入為御史中丞，遷侍中，又出為征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Early Xianning he entered as metropolitan censor, was promoted palace attendant, again went out as general who conquers the uncivilized.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning he became metropolitan censor, then palace attendant, then left the capital as general who conquers the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 太康初，為河南尹，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Early Taikang he was governor of Henan and granted the noble rank of secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taikang he served as governor of Henan and received a secondary marquisate within the passes.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸將歸籓，雄諫曰：「陛下子弟雖多，然有名望者少。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi, You, was about to return to his fief, Xiong remonstrated: "Your Majesty's sons and younger kin are many, yet few have renown.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qi, Sima You, was ordered to his fief, Xiang Xiong remonstrated: "Your sons are many, but few enjoy real prestige among the people."

sentences.zh: 齊王臥在京邑，所益實深，不可不思。

translations.literal: The prince of Qi lying in the capital benefits us very deeply—it must not go unconsidered."
translations.idiomatic: To keep the prince of Qi at the capital would do the dynasty deep good—think twice before you send him away."

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 雄固諫忤旨，起而徑出，遂以憤卒。

translations.literal: Xiong firmly remonstrated and offended the intent; he rose and went straight out, then died of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong pressed his advice until it angered the throne, then rose and walked out; he died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 弟匡，惠帝世為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Younger brother Kuang, in Emperor Hui's reign was general who guards the army.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiang Kuang became general who guards the army under Emperor Hui.

sentences.zh: 段灼，字休然，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Duan Zhuo, style Xiuran, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhuo, courtesy name Xiuran, was a native of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 世為西土著姓，果直有才辯。

translations.literal: For generations a great surname of the western lands, forthright and talented in disputation.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his clan had been a leading house of the west; he was blunt, upright, and a sharp debater.

sentences.zh: 少仕州郡，稍遷鄧艾鎮西司馬，從艾破蜀有功，封關內侯，累遷議郎。

translations.literal: In youth he served province and commandery, gradually promoted to Deng Ai's western army chief of staff; following Ai in breaking Shu he had merit, was enfeoffed secondary marquis within the passes, by stages promoted discussion gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He began in provincial posts, rose to chief of staff under Deng Ai, the general who guarded the west, followed him in the conquest of Shu, earned a secondary marquisate, and advanced to discussion gentleman.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，灼上疏追理艾曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu mounted the throne, Zhuo submitted a memorial reopening the case for Ai, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Duan Zhuo addressed a memorial to clear Deng Ai’s name:

sentences.zh: 故征西將軍鄧艾，心懷至忠，而荷反逆之名；

translations.literal: The late general who pacified the west, Deng Ai, cherished utmost loyalty yet bore the name of traitor;
translations.idiomatic: The late General Who Pacified the West, Deng Ai, was utterly loyal yet was labeled a traitor;

sentences.zh: 平定巴、蜀，而受三族之誅，臣竊悼之。

translations.literal: He pacified Ba and Shu yet received execution of the three clans—your subject privately mourns him.
translations.idiomatic: he conquered Ba and Shu yet suffered the three-clan extermination—I mourn him in private.

sentences.zh: 惜哉，言艾之反也！

translations.literal: Pity! That they spoke of Ai's rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: It is bitter to hear him called a rebel.

sentences.zh: 以艾性剛急，矜功伐善，而不能協同朋類，輕犯雅俗，失君子之心，故莫肯理之。

translations.literal: Because Ai by nature was hasty and harsh, boasted of merit and praised his own goodness, yet could not cooperate with peers, lightly offended refined custom, and lost gentlemen's hearts—therefore none would take up his cause.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was brusque and vain, could not work with colleagues, and offended polite opinion—so no one would speak for him.

sentences.zh: 臣敢昧死言艾所以不反之狀。

translations.literal: Your subject dares, blinding death, to speak the manner in which Ai did not rebel.
translations.idiomatic: I risk my life to show why Deng Ai could not have rebelled.

sentences.zh: 艾本屯田掌犢人，宣皇帝拔之于農吏之中，顯之於宰府之職。

translations.literal: Ai was originally a man who tended oxen for the state farms; Emperor Xuan pulled him from among farming clerks and displayed him in a ministerial office.
translations.idiomatic: Ai began as a herdsman on the military colonies; Emperor Xuan pulled him from the fields and set him among high ministers.

sentences.zh: 處內外之官，據文武之任，所在輒有名績，固足以明宣皇帝之知人矣。

translations.literal: Holding posts inner and outer, bearing civil and military charge, wherever he went he had famous achievements—this is enough to clarify Emperor Xuan's knowledge of men.
translations.idiomatic: In every civil and military post he distinguished himself—proof enough of Emperor Xuan’s eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 會值洮西之役，官兵失利，刺史王經困於圍城之中。

translations.literal: It happened the Taoxi campaign came: government troops were defeated; inspector Wang Jing was trapped inside a besieged city.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck at Taoxi and government troops were beaten, Inspector Wang Jing was trapped in a ring of siege.

sentences.zh: 當爾之時，二州危懼，隴右懍懍，幾非國家之有也。

translations.literal: In that time the two provinces were in peril and fear, the Longyou region trembled—almost it was no longer the state's possession.
translations.idiomatic: Both provinces trembled; the Longyou frontier nearly slipped from the state’s grasp.

sentences.zh: 先帝以為深憂重慮，思惟可以安邊殺敵莫賢于艾，故授之以兵馬，解狄道之圍。

translations.literal: The late emperor thought it deep worry and heavy care; in considering who could secure the borders and slay the foe none was worthier than Ai—therefore he entrusted him with arms and horses and lifted the siege on Didao.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor weighed every general and found none fitter to save the border than Deng Ai; he gave him troops and lifted the siege at Didao.

sentences.zh: 圍解，留屯上邽。

translations.literal: When the siege lifted, he remained stationed at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: After the relief he stayed to garrison Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 承官軍大敗之後，士卒破膽，將吏無氣，倉庫空虛，器械殫盡。

translations.literal: Following upon the government army's great defeat, soldiers were broken in courage, officers without spirit, storehouses empty, weapons exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The army had just been shattered: men were demoralized, officers listless, magazines empty, arms worn out.

sentences.zh: 艾欲積穀強兵，以待有事。

translations.literal: Ai wished to pile grain and strengthen troops to await events.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ai meant to store grain and rebuild the army against whatever came next.

sentences.zh: 是歲少雨，又為區種之法，手執耒耜，率先將士，所統萬數，而身不離僕虜之勞，親執士卒之役。

translations.literal: That year rain was sparse; again he applied the zoned-seeding method, hand holding plough and hoe, taking the lead before generals and soldiers—those under his command numbered in the tens of thousands, yet his body did not leave the toil of servants and captives, personally performing soldiers' drudgery.
translations.idiomatic: Rain failed that year; he introduced contour plowing, plough in hand, working ahead of his men—tens of thousands under him, yet he shared the labor of the lowest ranks.

sentences.zh: 故落門、段谷之戰，能以少擊多，摧破強賊，斬首萬計。

translations.literal: Therefore in the battles at Luomen and Duangu he could use few to strike many, smash strong bandits, and behead by the ten thousand count.
translations.idiomatic: Hence at Luomen and Duangu he shattered a stronger enemy with fewer troops and piled up ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 遂委艾以廟勝成圖，指授長策。

translations.literal: Thereupon they entrusted Ai with temple-victory charts, passing down long stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: The court then handed him the grand strategy drawn up in the temple.

sentences.zh: 艾受命忘身，龍驤麟振，前無堅敵。

translations.literal: Ai received orders, forgetting self—dragon-soaring, unicorn-shaking—nothing solid before him.
translations.idiomatic: He obeyed without thought for himself, swept forward like dragon or unicorn, and nothing could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 蜀地阻險，山高穀深，而艾步乘不滿二萬，束馬懸車，自投死地，勇氣陵雲，將士乘勢，故能使劉禪震怖，君臣面縛。

translations.literal: Shu terrain was blocked and steep, mountains high and valleys deep, yet Ai's foot and horse troops were fewer than twenty thousand; he bundled horses and suspended carriages, throwing himself onto deadly ground—courage overtopped the clouds, officers and soldiers rode the momentum; therefore he could make Liu Shan tremble in fear, ruler and ministers bound at the front.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was a maze of cliffs and defiles; Ai had fewer than twenty thousand foot and horse. He packed his horses on timbered paths and hurled himself into dead ground—courage that pierced the clouds carried his men until Liu Shan shook with terror and came out bound with his ministers.

sentences.zh: 軍不逾時，而巴、蜀蕩定，此艾固足以彰先帝之善任矣。

translations.literal: The army did not exceed the allotted time yet Ba and Shu were pacified—this indeed was enough to display the late emperor's good appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Ba and Shu fell within the allotted campaign—clear proof that the late emperor had chosen the right man.

sentences.zh: 艾功名已成，亦當書之竹帛，傳祚萬世。

translations.literal: Ai's merit and name were already accomplished—he also ought to be written on bamboo and silk, transmitted for myriad ages.
translations.idiomatic: His deeds deserved to be carved on bamboo and silk for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 七十老公，復何所求哉！

translations.literal: A seventy-year-old—what more could he seek!
translations.idiomatic: He was an old man of seventy—what could he still want?

sentences.zh: 艾以禪初降，遠郡未附，矯令承制，權安社稷。

translations.literal: Because Shan had just surrendered and distant commanderies had not submitted, Ai bent orders to act on delegated authority to settle the altars of soil and grain for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Shan had just yielded and outlying districts were still unsettled, Ai issued orders on his own authority to steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 雖違常科，有合古義，原心定罪，事可詳論。

translations.literal: Although it violated standing rules, it matched ancient meaning; judging by original intent the matter can be weighed in detail.
translations.idiomatic: That bent the rules, yet it matched classical precedent; judged by intent it deserves careful weighing, not summary condemnation.

sentences.zh: 故鎮西將軍鐘會，有吞天下之心，恐艾威名，知必不同，因其疑似，構成其事。

translations.literal: Therefore the general who garrisons the west, Zhong Hui, harbored a mind to swallow the world; fearing Ai's awe-inspiring fame, knowing they would surely not agree, he seized on ambiguity and framed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui, who garrisoned the west, meant to seize the empire; fearing Deng Ai’s fame and knowing they could not share power, he seized on ambiguities and framed him.

sentences.zh: 艾被詔書，即遣強兵，束身就縛，不敢顧望。

translations.literal: When Ai received the edict text he at once sent away strong troops, bound himself and submitted, not daring to look back.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict reached him, Ai disbanded his picked troops, bound himself, and surrendered without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 誠自知奉見先帝，必無當死之理也。

translations.literal: He truly knew that having audience with the late emperor there could be no ground for death.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted that once he faced the late emperor he would not die for it.

sentences.zh: 會受誅之後，艾參佐官屬、部曲將吏，愚戇相聚，自共追艾，破壞檻車，解其囚執。

translations.literal: After Hui met execution, Ai's staff assistants, subordinates, and cohort officers foolishly gathered together, themselves together chasing Ai, wrecked the prison cart, and freed his bonds.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui fell, Ai’s staff and soldiers—panicked fools—rushed after him, smashed his cage-cart, and freed his bonds.

sentences.zh: 艾在困地，是以狼狽失據。

translations.literal: Ai lay in straitened ground; therefore he was flustered and lost footing.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped and desperate, he lost every footing.

sentences.zh: 夫反非小事，若懷噁心，即當謀及豪傑，然後乃能興動大眾，不聞艾有腹心一人。

translations.literal: Now rebellion is no small matter—if one harbors evil intent one must first plot with heroes—only then can one stir the great host; one has not heard that Ai had a single confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion is no light thing: a rebel first gathers allies and only then moves the host—yet no one ever named a single confidant of Deng Ai’s.

sentences.zh: 臨死口無惡言，獨受腹背之誅，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: At death his mouth had no evil words—alone suffering execution front and back—is it not pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: At the block he spoke no treason—only to be cut down from front and rear. Can that fail to move pity?

sentences.zh: 故見之者垂涕，聞之者歎息。

translations.literal: Therefore those who saw wept tears; those who heard sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Witnesses wept; listeners sighed.

sentences.zh: 此賈誼所以慷慨于漢文，天下之事可為痛哭者，良有以也。

translations.literal: This is why Jia Yi was stirred with Han Wendi; that in affairs under heaven there are things fit for bitter weeping—truly there is reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Jia Yi broke his heart before Emperor Wen of Han—some wrongs in the world are worth bitter tears.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍興，闡弘大度，受誅之家，不拘敘用，聽艾立後，祭祀不絕。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's dragon-rise opens and spreads great magnanimity; houses that received execution are not barred from graded appointments—allowing Ai to establish an heir, so that sacrifice does not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has risen with generous grace: houses struck by punishment are not barred forever from office. Let Deng Ai have an heir and unbroken offerings.

sentences.zh: 昔秦人憐白起之無罪，吳人傷子胥之冤酷，皆為之立祠。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin people pitied Bai Qi lacking crime; Wu people hurt at Zixu's cruel injustice—each set up shrines for them.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin mourned Bai Qi’s innocence; the people of Wu grieved Wu Zixu’s cruelty—both won shrines.

sentences.zh: 天下之人為艾悼心痛恨，亦由是也。

translations.literal: The people under Heaven for Ai mourn in heart and hate in bitterness—it is the same case.
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven ache for Deng Ai with the same bitterness.

sentences.zh: 謂可聽艾門生故吏收艾屍柩，歸葬舊墓，還其田宅，以平蜀之功，繼封其後，使艾闔棺定諡，死無所恨。

translations.literal: I say you may allow Ai's students and former subordinates to gather his coffin and return it for burial on the old tomb, restore his fields and dwellings, and by merit in pacifying Shu enfeoff his posterity, so Ai may close the coffin and fix his posthumous title, dying without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Let his students and old aides recover his coffin, bury him on his family ground, return his lands, and enfeoff a descendant for the conquest of Shu so his posthumous name may be fixed and his ghost find peace.

sentences.zh: 赦冤魂于黃泉，收信義於後世，則天下徇名之士，思立功之臣，必投湯火，樂為陛下死矣！

translations.literal: To release a wronged soul in the yellow springs and gather trust and righteousness for later ages—then men under heaven who chase reputation and ministers who think to set merit will surely throw themselves into boiling water and fire and gladly die for Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: You would loose a wronged ghost under the earth and show posterity what faith means—then every man who seeks a name or a deed will gladly leap into fire and water for you."

sentences.zh: 帝省表，甚嘉其意。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and much praised his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and praised his intent.

sentences.zh: 灼後復陳時宜曰：

translations.literal: Zhuo later again presented the timely situation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhuo later submitted another memorial on policy:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天時不如地利，地利不如人和。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Heaven's timing is not as good as earth's advantage, and earth's advantage not as good as human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that heaven’s season is less telling than earth’s advantage, and earth’s advantage less telling than the harmony of men.

sentences.zh: 三里之城，五里之郭，圜圍而攻之，有不克者，此天時不如地利。

translations.literal: A city of three li, an outer wall of five li, if they besiege it in a circle yet sometimes cannot take it—this is Heaven's timing not as good as earth's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: A three-mile wall and five-mile outer rampart, ringed by attackers, may still hold—that shows season weaker than terrain.

sentences.zh: 城非不高，池非不深，穀非不多，兵非不利，委而去之，此地利不如人和。

translations.literal: The walls are not not high, the moat not not deep, grain not not abundant, weapons not not sharp—yet they abandon and leave it—this is earth's advantage not as good as human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Walls may be high, moats deep, grain piled high, weapons keen—yet the garrison flees—terrain is weaker than unity among men.

sentences.zh: 然古之王者，非不先推恩德，結固人心。

translations.literal: Yet ancient kings were not ones who failed first to extend favor and virtue and bind fast human hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of old always spread kindness first and bound the people’s hearts.

sentences.zh: 人心苟和，雖三里之城，五里之郭，不可攻也。

translations.literal: If human hearts are harmonized, though there be a city of three li and outer wall of five li, they cannot be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: When hearts are one, even a tiny citadel cannot be stormed.

sentences.zh: 人心不和，雖金城湯池，不能守也。

translations.literal: If human hearts are not harmonized, though there be metal walls and boiling moats, they cannot be defended.
translations.idiomatic: When hearts are divided, no golden fortress can be held.

sentences.zh: 臣推此以廣其義，舜彈五弦之琴，詠《南風》之詩，而天下自理，由堯人可比屋而封也。

translations.literal: Your subject pushes from this to broaden the meaning: Shun plucked a five-stringed lute and sang the 'South Wind' ode, and all under Heaven ordered itself—because Yao's people could have door-by-door enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: From this I infer: Shun played the five strings and sang the “South Wind,” and the realm ordered itself—because Yao’s people were as close as neighbors under one roof.

sentences.zh: 曩者多難，奸雄屢起，攪亂眾心，刀鋸相乘，流死之孤，哀聲未絕。

translations.literal: In recent times troubles have been many, scheming heroes have repeatedly risen, stirring the host of hearts; knives and saws succeeded one another; orphans of the flowing death—mourning voices have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Our own age has been a storm of usurpers; blades and saws have never rested; the wailing of the orphaned dead still rings in the ear.

sentences.zh: 故臣以為陛下當深思遠念，杜漸防萌，彈琴詠詩，垂拱而已。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject holds that Your Majesty ought to think deeply and plan afar, stop the gradual and guard the sprout, pluck the lute and sing the odes, fold hands and that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I urge Your Majesty to think far ahead, choke trouble at its root, pluck the lute, sing the classics, and rule with folded hands.

sentences.zh: 其要莫若推恩以協和黎庶，故推恩足以保四海，不推恩不足以保妻子。

translations.literal: The essential is none other than extending favor to harmonize the black-haired people; therefore extending favor suffices to preserve the four seas; not extending favor does not suffice to preserve wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: The heart of it is kindness to the common people: extend favor and you hold the realm; withhold it and you cannot guard your own household.

sentences.zh: 是故唐堯以親睦九族為先，周文以刑于寡妻為急，明王聖主莫不先親後疏，自近及遠。

translations.literal: Hence Tang Yao put friendly harmony of the nine kin first; Zhou Wen took model for the few wives as urgent; enlightened kings and sage lords put kin first and the distant second, from near to far.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yao began with harmony among the nine branches of kin; King Wen began with moral order in his own chamber; every sage king has cherished kin before strangers and the near before the far.

sentences.zh: 臣以為太宰、司徒、衛將軍三王宜留洛中鎮守，其餘諸王自州征足任者，年十五以上悉遣之國。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the grand tutor, minister of education, and general who guards the army—the three princes—ought to remain in Luoyang on guard; the remaining princes, those from the provinces full able in office, fifteen sui and above, all dispatch them to their states.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that the grand tutor, the minister of education, and the general who guards the army—the three princes—stay in Luoyang to anchor the capital; every other prince old enough to govern, from fifteen sui upward, should be sent to his fief.

sentences.zh: 為選中郎傅相，才兼文武，以輔佐之。

translations.literal: For them select gentleman-attendants, instructors, and chancellors—talented in both civil and military—to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Choose for each tutors and ministers who combine civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 聽于其國繕修兵馬，廣布恩信。

translations.literal: Allow in their states to repair arms and horses and spread favor and trust widely.
translations.idiomatic: Let them drill troops in their domains and spread trust among the people.

sentences.zh: 必撫下猶子，愛國如家，君臣分定，百世不遷，連城開地，為晉、魯、衛。

translations.literal: They will soothe the lower folk like sons, love the state as they love home; lord and subject portions are fixed for a hundred generations without shifting—even connected cities and opened lands become like Jin, Lu, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They will cherish the people like children and the realm like a home; lord and vassal will stand in fixed relation for generations, until wide domains recall the old houses of Jin, Lu, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 所謂磐石之宗，天下服其強矣。

translations.literal: What is called the clan of unshakeable stone—all under Heaven will submit to their strength.
translations.idiomatic: That is the true “bedrock of the state,” and the empire will feel its strength.

sentences.zh: 雖云割地，譬猶囊漏貯中，亦一家之有耳。

translations.literal: Although one speaks of dividing land, it is like leaking into the bag from the store—still within one household's possession.
translations.idiomatic: Though you speak of carving out fiefs, it is like pouring from one purse into another—all still within the royal house.

sentences.zh: 若慮後世強大，自可豫為制度，使得推恩以分子弟。

translations.literal: If you worry later generations grow too strong, you may beforehand set up institutions so they can extend favor to divide among sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: If you fear future strength, lay down rules now that princes must divide favor among sons and brothers.

sentences.zh: 如此則枝分葉布，稍自削小，漸使轉至萬國，亦後世之利，非所患也。

translations.literal: Then branches spread and leaves scatter, gradually themselves diminishing bit by bit, gradually shifting until ten thousand states—it also profits later ages, not something to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Branches will spread and power thin by degrees until you reach the model of myriad states of old—a boon to later reigns, not a danger.

sentences.zh: 昔在漢世，諸呂自疑，內有硃虛、東牟之親，外有諸侯九國之強，故不敢動搖。

translations.literal: Formerly in Han times the Lü group themselves doubted; inside they had the kin of Zhuxu and Dongmou; outside they had the strength of the feudatories' nine states—therefore they dared not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han the Lü feared to move because kin like Liu Zhang sat inside the capital and the nine feudatories pressed from without.

sentences.zh: 於今之宜，諸侯強大，是為太山之固。

translations.literal: For today's fit, the princes' strength is the solidity of Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: For today’s needs, strong princes are the dyke that steadies Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 非我族類，其心必異。

translations.literal: What is not our kind—their hearts must differ.
translations.idiomatic: Men who are not of our bone will not share our heart.

sentences.zh: 而魏法禁錮諸王，親戚隔絕，不祥莫大焉。

translations.literal: Yet Wei law shackled the princes and cut off kin—nothing more inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Wei code caged the princes and severed kin ties—nothing could be less auspicious.

sentences.zh: 間者無故又瓜分天下，立五等諸侯。

translations.literal: Lately without cause they again carved and partitioned all under Heaven, establishing nobles of the five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the realm was again carved up without need into the five ranks of nobility.

sentences.zh: 上不象賢，下不議功，而是非雜糅，例受茅土。

translations.literal: Above they do not model worthies; below they do not weigh merit—yet right and wrong are mixed and all alike receive fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Those above do not model the worthy, those below do not debate merit—yet right and wrong are jumbled and everyone alike receives a fief.

sentences.zh: 似權時之宜，非經久之制，將遂不改，此亦煩擾之人，漸亂之階也。

translations.literal: It seems a fit for the moment, not a lasting system; if it is left unchanged forever, this too is a ladder by which trouble will gradually climb.
translations.idiomatic: That may suit a moment’s expediency, not a lasting rule; if it stays forever unchanged, it will only breed resentment and creeping disorder.

sentences.zh: 夫國之興也，由於九族親睦，黎庶協和；

translations.literal: Now a state's rising comes from the nine kin being friendly and close and the black-haired people in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: States rise when the nine branches of kin live in harmony and the common people pull together.

sentences.zh: 其衰也，在於骨肉疏絕，百姓離心。

translations.literal: Its decline lies in flesh and bone cut off and the hundred surnames' hearts sundered.
translations.idiomatic: They fall when royal kin grow estranged and the people lose heart.

sentences.zh: 故夏邦不安，伊尹歸殷；

translations.literal: Therefore when the Xia realm was not secure, Yi Yin returned to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia tottered, Yi Yin went back to Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷邦不和，呂氏入周。

translations.literal: When the Yin realm was not harmonious, the Lü clan entered Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was divided, the Lü entered Zhou.

sentences.zh: 殷監在於夏後，去事之誡，誠來事之鑒也。

translations.literal: Yin's mirror lay in Xia's sequel—the warning of what is past is truly the mirror of what comes after.
translations.idiomatic: Yin took Xia’s fall as its mirror; yesterday’s lesson is tomorrow’s warning.

sentences.zh: 又陳曰：

translations.literal: Again he presented, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He went on:

sentences.zh: 昔伐蜀，募取涼州兵馬、羌胡健兒，許以重報，五千餘人，隨艾討賊，功皆第一。

translations.literal: Formerly in the Shu campaign they recruited Liangzhou horse troops and stalwart Qiang and Hu, promising heavy reward—more than five thousand followed Ai to strike the bandits, and their merit was all first rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was attacked, Liangzhou cavalry and Qiang and Hu fighters—over five thousand men promised rich reward—followed Deng Ai and every one earned first-class merit.

sentences.zh: 而《乙亥詔書》，州郡將督，不與中外軍同，雖在上功，無應封者。

translations.literal: Yet in the Yihai edict text, commandery and provincial commanders were not treated like inner and outer army officers; though merit was highest rank, none qualified for enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Yihai edict barred provincial commanders from the same rules as central army officers, so none could be enfeoffed no matter how high their merit.

sentences.zh: 唯金城太守楊欣所領兵，以逼江由之勢，得封者三十人。

translations.literal: Only the troops led by prefect of Jincheng Yang Xin, by pressure on Jiangyou's situation, had thirty men who received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yang Xin of Jincheng, pressing the Jiangyou front, won thirty of his men a fief.

sentences.zh: 自金城以西，非在欣部，無一人封者。

translations.literal: West of Jincheng, those not in Xin's division—none among them received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: West of Jincheng, outside Yang Xin’s command, not one soldier was enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 苟在中軍之例，雖下功必侯；

translations.literal: If they fell under central army regulations, though merit was low they must be marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Men under central army rules became marquises even on modest merit.

sentences.zh: 如在州郡，雖功高不封，非所謂近不重施，遠不遺恩之謂也。

translations.literal: If they were in province or commandery, though merit was high they were not enfeoffed—this is not what is called 'near does not double favors, far does not miss grace.'
translations.idiomatic: Provincial troops, however great their deeds, won no fiefs—hardly the promised ‘no favor withheld near or far.’

sentences.zh: 臣聞魚懸由於甘餌，勇夫死於重報。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard fish hang from sweet bait and brave men die for heavy reward.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet bait hooks fish; rich reward kills brave men.

sentences.zh: 故荊軻慕燕丹之義，專諸感闔閭之愛，匕首振于秦庭，吳刀耀於魚腹，視死如歸，豈不有由也哉！

translations.literal: Therefore Jing Ke admired Prince Dan of Yan's righteousness, Zhuan Zhu was moved by Helü's kindness—the dagger shook in Qin's court, the Wu blade flashed in the fish belly; they looked on death as going home—how could there be no cause!
translations.idiomatic: So Jing Ke died for Dan of Yan, Zhuan Zhu for King Helü—blade in the Qin court, sword in the fish—because they saw death as home for a cause they honored.

sentences.zh: 夫功名重賞，士之所競，不平致怨，由來久矣。

translations.literal: Now merit titles and heavy rewards are what gentlemen compete for; injustice breeds resentment—this has been long.
translations.idiomatic: Men fight for rank and bounty; injustice breeds grudges—it has always been so.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「屍鳩在桑，其子七兮。

translations.literal: The *Odes* say: "The shrike is on the mulberry; its chicks are seven.
translations.idiomatic: The *Book of Odes* says, ‘The shrike on the mulberry has seven chicks.’

sentences.zh: 淑人君子，其儀一兮。

translations.literal: The good man's gentleman—his deportment is one.
translations.idiomatic: ‘The good man’s bearing is one.’

sentences.zh: 」臣以為此等宜蒙爵封。

translations.literal: " Your subject holds that such men ought to receive noble rank and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: I say these soldiers deserve titles and fiefs.”

sentences.zh: 灼前後陳事，輒見省覽。

translations.literal: Zhuo's successive memorials were always examined and read.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhuo’s memorials were read and noted each time.

sentences.zh: 然身微宦孤，不見進序，乃取長假還鄉里。

translations.literal: Yet his person was lowly and his office isolated; he saw no advancement in order—therefore he took extended leave and returned to his village.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was small fry in a lonely post and never promoted, so he took long leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 臨去，遣息上表曰：

translations.literal: On the point of leaving, he sent his son to submit a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he had his son present a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣受恩三世，剖符守境，試用無績，沈伏數年，犬馬之力，無所復堪。

translations.literal: Your subject has received favor through three reigns, held tally and guarded territory, yet in trial service had no achievement and sank for several years; dog-and-horse strength has nothing further to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Three reigns have favored me; I bore a seal yet showed no merit and lay idle for years—I have no strength left to serve.

sentences.zh: 陛下弘廣納之聽，采狂夫之言，原臣侵官之罪，不問幹忤之愆，天地恩厚，於臣足矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty opens wide the ear that accepts, takes a madman's words, forgives your subject's crime of overstepping office, and does not ask fault for offense—Heaven and earth's favor is enough for your subject.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty hears all counsel, heeds a madman’s plea, forgives my intrusion, and punishes no blunt offense—your grace fills heaven and earth for me.

sentences.zh: 臣聞忠臣之于其君，猶孝子之於其親：進則有欣然之慶，非貪官也；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that a loyal minister toward his lord is like a filial son toward his parents: in advancing there is glad rejoicing—not greed for office.
translations.idiomatic: A loyal minister toward his ruler is like a filial son toward his parents: to advance brings joy, not greed for rank.

sentences.zh: 退則有戚然之憂，非懷祿也。

translations.literal: In retiring there is sorrowful care—not cherishing stipend.
translations.idiomatic: To withdraw brings grief, not clinging to salary.

sentences.zh: 其意在於不忘光君榮親，情所不能已已者也。

translations.literal: The intent lies in not forgetting to glorify the lord and honor kin—what emotion could restrain itself!
translations.idiomatic: The heart only wants to bring honor to ruler and kin—how could feeling hold back?

sentences.zh: 臣伏自悼，私懷至恨：生長荒裔，而久在外任，自還抱疾，未嘗覲見，陛下竟不知臣何人，此臣之恨一也。

translations.literal: Your subject prostrate grieves, privately cherishing utmost regret: born and reared on a remote frontier, long stationed in outer posts, since returning bearing illness never having had audience—Your Majesty to the end does not know what manner of man your subject is—this is your subject's first regret.
translations.idiomatic: I mourn five private griefs: reared on the frontier, long abroad, ill since my return, never granted audience—you do not even know who I am.

sentences.zh: 遭運會之世，值有事之時，而不能垂功名於竹帛，此臣之恨二也。

translations.literal: Meeting a fated age, encountering a time of affairs, yet unable to hang merit and name on bamboo and silk—this is your subject's second regret.
translations.idiomatic: Second, I lived in an age of deeds yet left no name on the bamboo slips.

sentences.zh: 逮事聖明之君，而尪悴羸劣，陳力又不能，當歸死於地下，此臣之恨三也。

translations.literal: Having caught service with a sagely and enlightened lord, yet wizened, wasted, and weak, unable to set forth strength—ought to return and die under the earth—this is your subject's third regret.
translations.idiomatic: Third, I served a sage emperor yet am too frail to give my strength—I should die in the dust.

sentences.zh: 哀二親早亡隕，兄弟並凋喪，孝敬無復施於家門，此臣之恨四也。

translations.literal: Grieving that both parents died early, brothers together withered—filial respect can no longer be practiced at the gate—this is your subject's fourth regret.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, my parents died young and my brothers are gone—I can no longer show filial piety at home.

sentences.zh: 夏之日忽以過，冬之夜尋復來，人生百歲，尚以為不足，而臣中年嬰災，此臣之恨五也。

translations.literal: Summer's day suddenly passes, winter's night soon returns; human life at a hundred years they still deem not enough—yet your subject in mid-years met disaster—this is your subject's fifth regret.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, summer races by and winter returns; even a hundred years seem short, yet midlife brought me ruin.

sentences.zh: 慚日月之所養，愧昊蒼而無報，此臣之所以懷五恨而歎息，臨歸路而自悼者也。

translations.literal: Ashamed at what sun and moon nurture, shamed before vast Heaven without repayment—this is why your subject harbors five regrets and sighs, and on the road of return grieves for himself.
translations.idiomatic: I blush before sun and moon and owe Heaven a debt I cannot pay—these five regrets wring my heart as I take the road home.

sentences.zh: 語有之曰：「華言虛也，至言實也，苦言藥也，甘言疾也。

translations.literal: The saying has it: "Flowery words are empty; utmost words are real; bitter words are medicine; sweet words are disease.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says, ‘Flowery speech is hollow, straight speech is true, bitter words are medicine, sweet words are poison.’

sentences.zh: 」臣欲言天下太平，而靈龜神狐未見，仙芝萐莆未生，麒麟未遊乎靈禽之囿，鳳皇未儀於太極之庭，此臣之所以不敢華言而為佞者也。

translations.literal: " Your subject wishes to speak that all under Heaven is at peace, yet spirit tortoise and divine fox have not appeared, immortal zhi and shantao have not sprouted; the qilin does not roam the park of numinous birds, the phoenix does not display pattern at the supreme ultimate court—this is why your subject dares not speak flowery words and act the flatterer.
translations.idiomatic: I would gladly say the realm is at peace, yet no tortoise omen, no spirit fox, no lucky fungi, no qilin in the royal park, no phoenix at court—so I dare not mouth pretty lies like a sycophant.”

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖初定天下，于時戍卒婁敬上書諫曰：「陛下取天下不與成周同，而欲比靈斯成周，臣竊以為不侔。

translations.literal: Formerly when Han Gaozu first settled all under Heaven, at that time a garrison soldier Lou Jing submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your Majesty took all under Heaven not as with completed Zhou, yet you wish to compare auspiciously with completed Zhou—your subject privately holds it not a match.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu had just won the empire, the soldier Lou Jing warned him, ‘You won the realm differently from the Zhou founders; to claim their omens is a poor fit.’

sentences.zh: 」於是漢祖感悟，深納其言，賜姓為劉氏。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Han Gaozu was moved and deeply took in his words, bestowing the surname Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu listened, took the point to heart, and gave Lou Jing the imperial surname.

sentences.zh: 又顧謂陸賈曰：「為我著秦所以亡，而吾所以得之者。

translations.literal: Again he turned and told Lu Jia: "For me write why Qin perished and how I obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: He told Lu Jia, ‘Write me how Qin fell and how I rose.’

sentences.zh: 」賈乃作《新語》之書，述敘前世成敗，以為勸戒。

translations.literal: " Jia thereupon composed the book *New Discourses*, narrating former ages' success and failure, to serve as encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jia wrote the *New Discourses*, tracing past rise and fall as a mirror.

sentences.zh: 又田肯建一言之計，非親子弟莫可使王齊者，而受千金之賜。

translations.literal: Again Tian Ken offered a single-word plan—unless close younger kin, none may be made king of Qi—and received a thousand-cash reward.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ken urged that only kin could hold Qi as king and earned a thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 故世稱漢祖之寬明博納，所以能成帝業也。

translations.literal: Therefore the age calls Han Gaozu's broad clarity and broad acceptance—this is why he could complete the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The world praises Gaozu’s openness—how else could he build an empire?

sentences.zh: 今之言世者，皆曰堯舜復興，天下已太平矣。

translations.literal: Today's speakers of the age all say Yao and Shun are reborn and all under Heaven is already at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Today everyone cries that Yao and Shun are back and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為未，亦竊有所勸焉。

translations.literal: Your subject alone holds it not yet so, and also privately has something to urge.
translations.idiomatic: I alone do not believe it, and I have a warning to offer.

sentences.zh: 且百王垂制，聖賢吐言，來事之明鑒也。

translations.literal: Moreover the hundred kings' hanging institutions and sages' uttered words are the bright mirror of what comes after.
translations.idiomatic: The laws the kings left and the sages spoke are the clearest mirror for what follows.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「堯不能以天下與舜，則舜之有天下也，天與之也。

translations.literal: Mencius said: "Yao could not give all under Heaven to Shun—then Shun's having all under Heaven was Heaven giving it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, ‘Yao could not simply hand the realm to Shun; Heaven gave it to him.’

sentences.zh: 昔舜為相，堯崩，三年之喪畢，舜避堯之子于南河，天下諸侯朝覲者、獄訟者，不之堯之子而之舜。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun was minister; when Yao died, after the three-year mourning was finished, Shun yielded to Yao's son at the south river—of all under Heaven's feudal lords those who came to court and those who brought suits did not go to Yao's son but to Shun.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun yielded to Yao’s son south of the river, lords and litigants still flocked to Shun, not to the son.

sentences.zh: 舜曰天也，乃之中國，踐天子位焉。

translations.literal: Shun said it was Heaven, and thereupon entered the central domain and trod the Son of Heaven's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Shun called it Heaven’s will and took the throne in the central plain.

sentences.zh: 若居堯之宮，逼堯之子，非天所與者也。

translations.literal: If he had dwelt in Yao's palace and pressed Yao's son, that would not be what Heaven gave.
translations.idiomatic: Had he seized Yao’s palace and forced the son, that would not have been Heaven’s gift.”

sentences.zh: 」曩昔西有不臣之蜀，東有僭號之吳，三主鼎足，並稱天子。

translations.literal: " Formerly in the west there was Shu that did not submit as minister; in the east Wu that usurped the title—three lords tripod-footed, each calling himself Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu defied the west and Wu claimed the east—three rulers each styled himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝率萬乘之眾，受禪於靡陂，而自以德同唐、虞，以為漢獻即是古之堯，自謂即是今之舜，乃謂孟柯、孫卿不通禪代之變，遂作禪代之文，刻石垂戒，班示天下，傳之後世，亦安能使將來君子皆曉然心服其義乎！

translations.literal: Wei Wendi led the host of ten thousand chariots, received abdication at Fanpi, yet by himself thought his virtue matched Tang and Yu, took Han Xiandi as the Yao of antiquity, himself as today's Shun—and then said Meng Ke and Sun Qing did not understand abdication's changes; thereupon he composed abdication texts, carved stone to hang warning, promulgated all under Heaven, transmitted to later ages—how could that make gentlemen of later times all clearly submit in heart to his meaning!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wendi accepted abdication at Fanpi yet styled himself another Yao or Shun, mocked Mencius and Xunzi for not grasping abdition, carved his doctrine in stone—how could that make later ages honestly assent?

sentences.zh: 然魏文徒希慕堯、舜之名，推新集之魏，欲以同于唐、虞之盛，忽骨肉之恩，忘籓屏之固，竟不能使四海賓服，混一皇化，而于時群臣莫有諫者，不其過矣哉！

translations.literal: Yet Wei Wendi vainly admired Yao and Shun's names, pushed the freshly gathered Wei, wished to match Tang and Yu's flourishing, neglected flesh-and-bone grace, forgot the screen-wall's solidity, and in the end could not make the four seas guest-submit and merge the imperial transformation—yet at that time among the host of ministers none remonstrated—is it not excessive fault!
translations.idiomatic: He aped Yao and Shun while weakening kin who should shield the throne, never unified the realm, and no minister dared remonstrate—was that not a grave fault?

sentences.zh: 孫卿曰：「堯、舜禪讓，是不然矣。

translations.literal: Sun Qing said: "Yao and Shun's abdication is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi said, ‘So-called abdication by Yao and Shun is not as told.’

sentences.zh: 天下者，至重也，非至強莫之能任；

translations.literal: All under Heaven is the supremely heavy—not the supremely strong cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is supremely heavy—only the strongest can bear it.

sentences.zh: 至大也，非至辯莫之能分；

translations.literal: It is the supremely great—not the supremely eloquent cannot divide it.
translations.idiomatic: It is supremely vast—only the most eloquent can parse it.

sentences.zh: 至眾也，非至明莫之能見。

translations.literal: It is the supremely numerous—not the supremely bright cannot see it.
translations.idiomatic: Its affairs are supremely many—only the clearest eye can see them.

sentences.zh: 此三至者，非聖人莫之能盡。

translations.literal: These three ultimates—none but a sage can exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: None but a sage can master those three heights.”

sentences.zh: 」由此言之，孫卿、孟軻亦各有所不取焉。

translations.literal: " From this speaking, Sun Qing and Meng Ke also each have what they do not take.
translations.idiomatic: So Mencius and Xunzi each withhold assent from some tales.

sentences.zh: 陛下受禪，從東府入西宮，兵刃耀天，旌旗翳日。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received abdication, from the eastern offices entered the western palace—blades of arms dazzled the sky, banners and flags eclipsed the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty moved from the eastern palace to the western hall under glittering arms and banners that hid the sun.

sentences.zh: 雖應天順人，同符唐、虞，然法度損益，則亦不異于昔魏文矣，故宜資三至以強制之。

translations.literal: Although answering Heaven and following men, matching tally with Tang and Yu, yet in laws and measures' loss and gain it is also not different from former Wei Wendi—therefore one ought to borrow the three ultimates to strengthen and control it.
translations.idiomatic: You match Heaven and the people like Tang and Yu, yet your legal changes differ little from Wei Wendi’s—you should use Xunzi’s three tests to steady the rule.

sentences.zh: 而今諸王有立國之名，而無襟帶之實。

translations.literal: Now the various princes have the name of founding states yet lack the reality of belt-and-collar closeness.
translations.idiomatic: The princes bear the title of state founders but lack real ties that bind the capital.

sentences.zh: 又蜀地有自然之險，是曆世奸雄之所窺覦，逋逃之所聚也，而無親戚子弟之守，此豈深思遠慮，杜漸防萌者乎！

translations.literal: Further Shu territory has nature's steepness—it is what age after age of scheming heroes has coveted and where fugitives gather—yet there are no kin younger kinsmen guarding it—is this deep thought and far planning, stopping the gradual and guarding the sprout!
translations.idiomatic: Shu’s natural defenses have always tempted rebels and outlaws, yet no imperial kin garrison them—where is the long-term plan to choke trouble at its root?

sentences.zh: 昔漢文帝據已成之業，六合同風，天下一家。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Wendi relied on already completed enterprise; the six directions shared one wind, all under Heaven one house.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi inherited a finished realm: the empire breathed as one.

sentences.zh: 而賈誼上疏陳當時之勢，猶以為譬如抱火厝於積薪之下，而寢其上，火未及然，因謂之安。

translations.literal: Yet Jia Yi submitted a memorial stating the situation of the time, still thinking it like embracing fire and placing it under piled kindling then sleeping atop it—fire had not yet caught, and for that reason he called it safe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jia Yi warned him it was like sleeping on kindling with live coals—safe only because the flames had not yet caught.

sentences.zh: 此言誠存不忘亡，安不忘亂者也。

translations.literal: These words truly preserve not forgetting perish, in peace not forgetting turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: That is the mind that remembers ruin in survival and danger in calm.

sentences.zh: 然臣之慺慺，亦竊願陛下居安思危，無曰高高在上，常念臨深之義，不忘履冰之戒。

translations.literal: Yet your subject's earnest dullness also privately wishes Your Majesty in peace to think of peril, not to say 'I am high above,' always to keep in mind the meaning of standing over a deep pit, not to forget the warning of treading on ice.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, in peace, to think of peril—not to feel too high above the world, to remember the pit at your feet and the thin ice under them.

sentences.zh: 盡除魏世之弊法，綏以新政之大化，使萬邦欣欣，喜戴洪惠，昆蟲草木，咸蒙恩澤。

translations.literal: Utterly remove Wei's flawed laws, soothe with the great transformation of new government, so that myriad regions rejoice, gladly bearing vast favor—insects and plants alike receive the moisture of grace.
translations.idiomatic: Sweep away Wei’s bad statutes, spread a new humane rule until every land rejoices, down to insect and plant.

sentences.zh: 朝廷詠康哉之歌，山藪無伐檀之人，此固天下所視望者也。

translations.literal: The court chants the song of peace; in hills and marshes there are none who fell sandalwood—this is indeed what all under Heaven look up to and hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Let the court sing the ‘Kangzai’ hymns and leave no woodcutters grumbling in the hills—that is what the world hopes to see.

sentences.zh: 陛下自初踐阼，發無諱之詔，置箴諫之官，赫然寵異諤諤之臣，以明好直言之信，恐陳事者知直言之不用，皆杜口結舌，祥瑞亦曷由來哉！

translations.literal: From Your Majesty's first treading of the throne you issued an edict without taboo, set up officials for needle admonition, brilliantly favored and distinguished ministers who were forthright—to make clear faith in loving straight speech—lest those who state affairs know straight speech is unused, all seal mouths and bind tongues—how then could auspicious omens come!
translations.idiomatic: From your accession you welcomed blunt counsel—if frank men fall silent for fear, how will auspicious omens ever arrive?

sentences.zh: 臣無陸生之才，不在顧問之地，蓋聞主聖臣直，義在於有犯無隱。

translations.literal: Your subject lacks Lu Sheng's talent, is not in the place of counsel—yet has heard the lord sage and ministers straight, righteousness lying in offending where there is nothing hidden.
translations.idiomatic: I am no Lu Jia, not in your inner council, yet I know: a sage ruler wants straight ministers who hide nothing.

sentences.zh: 臣不惟疏遠，未信而言，敢曆論前代隆名之君及亡敗之主廢興所由，又博陳舉賢之路，廣開養老之制，崇必信之道，又張設議者之難，凡五事以聞。

translations.literal: Your subject does not think only of remoteness, nor of being unbelieved yet speaking—dares to traverse discussion of former ages' lords of lofty name and ruined lords' rise and fall causes, again broadly to set out the road of raising worthies, broadly to open systems for nurturing the aged, to exalt the way of must-trust, again to spread the debaters' difficulties—in all five matters to report.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am remote and little trusted, I dare trace why famous kings rose and tyrants fell, lay out paths to find talent, care for the aged, keep faith, and answer objections—five themes in all.

sentences.zh: 臣之所言，皆直陳古今已行故事，非新聲異端也。

translations.literal: What your subject speaks all straightly states old and present already practiced precedents—not new sounds or strange doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Everything I cite is precedent from past and present, not novel theory.

sentences.zh: 辭義實淺，不足採納。

translations.literal: The wording's meaning is truly shallow—not worth accepting.
translations.idiomatic: My words are plain and may not deserve your ear.

sentences.zh: 然臣私心，誠謂有可發起覺悟遺忘。

translations.literal: Yet your subject's private heart truly holds that there is what can rouse and awaken forgetfulness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I believe they can jog memory and wake indifference.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察臣愚忠，湣臣狂直，無使天下以言者為戒。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to inspect your subject's foolish loyalty, pity your subject's mad straightness, and not make all under Heaven take speakers as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Please see my clumsy loyalty, forgive my blunt zeal, and do not teach the world to fear speaking.

sentences.zh: 疾痛增篤，退念桑梓之詩，惟狐死之義，輒取長休，歸近墳墓。

translations.literal: Illness and pain grow graver; retiring I recall the 'mulberry and catalpa' poem, think only of the fox's dying-at-home meaning—thereupon taking long rest, returning near tombs.
translations.idiomatic: My sickness worsens; I think of returning home like the poem says, like the fox that dies facing its burrow—I take long leave to lie near my parents’ graves.

sentences.zh: 顧瞻宮闕，系情皇極，不勝丹款，遣息穎表言。

translations.literal: Looking back at palace gates, my heart ties to the pole star—unable to bear crimson sincerity, sending son Ying to submit words in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I gaze toward the palace yet my heart stays with the throne; unable to come myself, I send my son Ying with this memorial.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：臣聞善有章也，著在經典；

translations.literal: The first says: Your subject has heard good has its pattern—it is set out in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: First: I have heard good deeds are patterned—they stand written in the classics.

sentences.zh: 惡有罰也，戒在刑書。

translations.literal: Evil has its punishments—it is warned in the penal writings.
translations.idiomatic: Evil has its punishments—they are warned in the penal codes.

sentences.zh: 上自遠古，下洎秦、漢，其明王霸主及亡國暗君，故可得而稱；

translations.literal: Above from high antiquity, down to Qin and Han—their enlightened kings, hegemonic lords, and perished-state dark lords—thus can be named.
translations.idiomatic: From high antiquity through Qin and Han one can name bright kings, hegemons, and dark lords who lost their states.

sentences.zh: 至於忠蹇賢相及佞諂奸臣，亦可得而言。

translations.literal: As for loyal blunt worthy chancellors and fawning wicked ministers—also can be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: One can also name blunt loyal ministers and flattering traitors.

sentences.zh: 故朝有諤諤盡規之臣，無不昌也；

translations.literal: Therefore courts that have forthright ministers who exhaust remonstration—none fail to flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Courts with blunt remonstrators always flourish.

sentences.zh: 任用阿諛唯唯之士，無不亡也。

translations.literal: Those who employ fawning yes-men—none fail to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Courts that favor sycophants always fall.

sentences.zh: 是有國者皆欲求忠以自輔，舉賢以自佐；

translations.literal: Therefore those who possess a state all seek loyalty to assist themselves and raise worthies to help themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Every ruler wants loyal help and worthy ministers.

sentences.zh: 而亡國破家者相繼，皆由任失其人。

translations.literal: Yet ruined states and broken houses follow one another—all from appointing the wrong men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ruin follows ruin because the wrong men were chosen.

sentences.zh: 所謂賢者不賢，忠者不忠也。

translations.literal: What is called worthy is not worthy; what is called loyal is not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Men called worthy prove unworthy; men called loyal prove disloyal.

sentences.zh: 臣謹言前任賢所由興，任不肖所以亡者。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully speaks the former: by what raising worthies rises; by what employing unworthies perishes.
translations.idiomatic: I shall show how worthies built states and how unworthies destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 堯之末年，四凶在朝而不去，八元在家而不舉，然致天平地寧，四門穆穆，其功固在重華之為相。

translations.literal: In Yao's late years the four fiends were at court yet not removed, the eight good ones were at home yet not raised—yet he brought heaven flat and earth still, the four gates august—his achievement indeed lay in Chonghua's being minister.
translations.idiomatic: Late Yao kept four villains at court and ignored eight talents, yet the realm stayed calm because Shun served as minister.

sentences.zh: 夏癸放於鳴條，商辛梟於牧野，此俱萬乘之主，而國滅身擒，由不能屬任賢相，用婦人之言，荒淫無道，肆志沈宴，作靡靡之樂，長夜之飲，於是登糟丘，臨酒池，觀牛飲，望肉林，龍逢忠而被害，比干諫而剖心，天下之所以歸惡者也。

translations.literal: Xia Gui was banished at Mingtiao; Shang Xin was displayed at Muye—these were both lords of ten thousand chariots, yet state perished and body captured, from inability to delegate to worthy chancellors, using women's words, dissolute without the Way, indulging will in deep feasts, making decadent music, long-night drinking—thereupon mounting the lees-mound, overlooking the wine pool, watching ox-drink, gazing at the meat forest—Long Feng loyal yet harmed, Bi Gan remonstrating yet heart carved—this is why all under Heaven turned their hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Jie of Xia and Zhou of Yin were both emperors yet lost all—because they spurned good ministers, listened to women, drowned in wine and debauch, killed Long Feng and Bi Gan—so the world turned on them.

sentences.zh: 太甲暴虐，顛覆湯之典制，於是伊尹放之桐宮，而能改悔反善，三年而後歸於亳。

translations.literal: Taijia was violent and cruel, overturning Tang's institutions—thereupon Yi Yin banished him to the Tong palace, yet he was able to change regret and return to good; after three years he returned to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Taijia was cruel and broke Tang’s laws; Yi Yin exiled him to Tong until he repented, then welcomed him back to Bo after three years.

sentences.zh: 既已放而復還，殷道微而復興，諸侯咸服，號稱太宗，實賴阿衡之盡忠也。

translations.literal: Already banished yet again returned, Yin way slight yet again rose, feudal lords all submitted, styled Grand Temple—this truly relied on the steward's exhausting loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Yin revived through that exile; lords submitted and Taijia became ‘Grand Temple’—thanks to Yi Yin’s steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 周室既衰，諸侯並爭，天王微弱，政遂陵遲。

translations.literal: When Zhou house had declined, feudal lords together contended, the heavenly king was feeble, government thereupon slid downward.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou decayed, lords warred and the king grew weak.

sentences.zh: 齊桓公，淫亂之主耳；

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi was a lord of dissolute chaos only.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi was a lecher at heart.

sentences.zh: 然所以能九合一匡之功，有尊周之名，誠管夷吾之力。

translations.literal: Yet the reason he could achieve nine gatherings and one rectification's merit, have the name of honoring Zhou, was truly Guan Yiwu's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he united the lords and honored Zhou because of Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 及其死也，蟲流出門，豈非任豎貂之過乎！

translations.literal: When he died, maggots flowed out the door—is it not fault in employing Shu Diao!
translations.idiomatic: When he died maggots crawled from his door—price of trusting Shu Diao.

sentences.zh: 且一桓公之身，得管仲，其功如彼；

translations.literal: Moreover in one Huan's body—obtaining Guan Zhong, his merit was like that.
translations.idiomatic: The same Huan with Guan Zhong wrought greatness.

sentences.zh: 用豎貂，其亂如此。

translations.literal: Employing Shu Diao, his chaos was like this.
translations.idiomatic: With Shu Diao he brought chaos.

sentences.zh: 夫榮辱存亡，實在所任，可不審哉！

translations.literal: Now glory and shame, survival and perdition, truly lie in whom you appoint—can you not examine!
translations.idiomatic: Glory, shame, life, and ruin hang on appointments—choose with care!

sentences.zh: 秦本伯翳之後，微微小邑，至秦仲始大，有車馬禮樂侍御之好焉。

translations.literal: Qin was originally descendant of Boyi, a tiny small town; by Qin Zhong it first grew large, having the fondness for chariots, horses, ritual, music, and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Qin began as a tiny clan of Boyi’s line; under Qin Zhong it grew fond of chariots, rites, and music.

sentences.zh: 自穆公至於始皇，皆能留心待賢，遠求異士，招由余於西戎，致五羖于宛市，取丕豹于晉鄉，迎蹇叔于宗裏。

translations.literal: From Duke Mu down to First Emperor, all were able to set mind on awaiting worthies, seek strange shi from afar, summon You Yu from western Rong, bring five black rams from Wan market, take Pi Bao from Jin village, welcome Jian Shu from Zong hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: From Duke Mu to the First Emperor every ruler sought talent far and near—You Yu from the Rong, five rams from Wan, Pi Bao from Jin, Jian Shu from his hamlet.

sentences.zh: 由是四方雄俊繼踵而至，故能世為強國，吞滅諸侯，奄有天下，兼稱皇帝，由謀臣之助也。

translations.literal: Thereupon heroes of the four quarters came in succession; therefore they could generation after generation be a strong state, swallow and destroy feudal lords, cover all under Heaven, and jointly style themselves emperor—through plotting ministers' help.
translations.idiomatic: Heroes flocked in; generation on generation Qin grew strong, swallowed rivals, seized the throne—thanks to wise advisers.

sentences.zh: 道化未淳，崩於沙丘。

translations.literal: The transforming way was not yet pure; he collapsed at Sand Dunes.
translations.idiomatic: The moral order was still crude when the First Emperor died at Sand Dunes.

sentences.zh: 胡亥乘虐，用詐自悮，不能弘濟統緒，克成堂構，而乃殘賊仁義，毒流黔首。

translations.literal: Er Shi rode cruelty, used deceit to mislead himself, unable broadly to aid the line of succession and complete the hall's frame—instead he mutilated benevolence and righteousness, poison spreading to the black-haired.
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor rode cruelty and fraud, ruined the succession, and butchered the good until poison spread to every commoner.

sentences.zh: 故陳勝、吳廣，奮臂大呼，而天下回應。

translations.literal: Therefore Chen Sheng and Wu Guang raised arms and great cried, and all under Heaven turned in answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang raised a cry and the realm answered.

sentences.zh: 於是趙高逆亂，閻樂承指，二世窮迫，自戮望夷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao Gao rebelled in disorder; Yan Le received his finger; the Second Emperor was pressed to the limit and killed himself at Wangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao seized power, Yan Le struck, and the Second Emperor died at Wangyi.

sentences.zh: 子嬰雖立，去帝為王，孤危無輔，四旬而亡。

translations.literal: Though Ziying was set up, he removed emperor title to be king, orphaned and perilous without aid—in forty days he perished.
translations.idiomatic: Ziying lasted forty days, king in name alone, with no support.

sentences.zh: 此由邪臣擅命，指鹿為馬，所以速秦之禍也。

translations.literal: This came from wicked ministers monopolizing orders, pointing at a deer and calling it a horse—therefore hastening Qin's disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked ministers called deer horse and hastened Qin’s fall.

sentences.zh: 秦失其鹿，豪傑競逐，項羽既得而失之，其咎在烹韓生，而范增之謀不用。

translations.literal: Qin lost its deer; heroes raced to seize it; Xiang Yu obtained it yet lost it—his fault lay in boiling Han Sheng and not using Fan Zeng's plans.
translations.idiomatic: Qin lost the realm; Xiang Yu seized it then lost it—boiling Han Sheng and spurning Fan Zeng were his faults.

sentences.zh: 假令羽既距項伯之邪說，斬沛公於鴻門，都咸陽以號令諸侯，則天下無敵矣。

translations.literal: Suppose Yu had rejected Xiang Bo's crooked counsel, cut Pei Gong at Hongmen, and capital at Xianyang to command the feudal lords—then none under Heaven could have matched him.
translations.idiomatic: Had he killed Liu Bang at Hongmen and ruled from Xianyang, none could have stood against him.

sentences.zh: 而羽距韓生之忠諫，背范增之深計，自謂霸王之業已定，都彭城，還故鄉，為晝被文繡，此蓋世俗兒女之情耳，而羽榮之。

translations.literal: Yet Yu rejected Han Sheng's loyal remonstrance, turned his back on Fan Zeng's deep plans, himself thought the hegemon's enterprise already fixed, capital at Pengcheng, returning to his old village, by day wearing patterned embroidery—this is merely the feeling of vulgar sons and daughters—yet Yu gloried in it.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he scorned good counsel, trusted his own pride, went home to Pengcheng in silks like a provincial fool—and gloried in it.

sentences.zh: 是故五載為漢所擒，至此尚不知覺悟，乃曰「天亡我，非戰之罪」，甚痛矣哉！

translations.literal: Therefore in five years he was captured by Han—to this point still not awakened, then saying 'Heaven destroys me, it is not war's fault'—how bitter indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Five years later Han seized him; still he cried ‘Heaven, not my warcraft’—how blind!

sentences.zh: 且夫士之歸仁，猶水之歸下，禽之走曠野，故曰「為川驅魚者獺也，為藪驅雀者鸇也，為湯、武驅人者桀、紂也。

translations.literal: Moreover gentlemen's turning to benevolence is like water's flowing downward, birds' fleeing to the wild—therefore it is said 'What drives fish to the deep is the otter; what drives sparrows to the marsh is the sparrowhawk; what drives men to Tang and Wu is Jie and Zhou.'
translations.idiomatic: Men flock to benevolence as water runs downhill—Jie and Zhou drove the people to Tang and Wu.

sentences.zh: 」漢高祖起于布衣，提三尺之刃而取天下，用六國之資，無唐、虞之禪，豈徒賴良、平之奇謀，盡英雄之智力而已乎，亦由項 氏為驅人也。

translations.literal: " Han Gaozu rose from common cloth, grasped a three-foot blade and took all under Heaven, used the six states' resources, lacked Tang and Yu's abdication—how could he rely only on Liang and Ping's strange plans and exhaust heroes' wit and strength—also because the Xiang clan drove men for him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rose from the ranks with a sword and the wealth of the six states—he needed more than Zhang Liang’s plots; Xiang Yu drove the world into his arms.

sentences.zh: 子孫承基二百餘年，逮成帝委政舅家，使權勢外移。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons inherited the base over two hundred years—down to Chengdi delegating power to the maternal uncles' house, causing authority to shift outward.
translations.idiomatic: Two centuries later Chengdi handed power to his uncles and let authority leak outward.

sentences.zh: 安昌侯張禹者，漢之三公，成帝保傅也，帝親幸其家，拜禹床下，深問天災人事。

translations.literal: Marquis Anchang Zhang Yu was Han's three dukes, Chengdi's tutor; the emperor personally favored his house, bowed below Zhang Yu's couch, deeply asking about heaven's disasters and human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu, tutor to the throne, received the emperor bowing at his couch while Chengdi asked omens of state.

sentences.zh: 禹當惟大臣之節，為社稷深慮，忠言嘉謀，陳其災患，則王氏不得專權寵，王莽無緣乘勢位，遂托雲龍而登天衢，令漢祚中絕也。

translations.literal: Yu ought to have thought of a great minister's integrity, for the altars of soil and grain planned deeply, stated loyal words and fine plans, set forth disasters—then the Wang clan could not monopolize favor and power, Wang Mang would have had no chance to ride momentum and position, mount cloud-dragon and climb heaven's avenue, making Han mandate break mid-way.
translations.idiomatic: Had Zhang Yu spoken truly, the Wang clan could not have seized power and Wang Mang could never have usurped Han.

sentences.zh: 禹佞諂不忠，挾懷私計，徒低仰于五侯之間，苟取容媚而已。

translations.literal: Yu fawned and was not loyal, hugged private schemes, merely bobbed among the five marquises, seeking only to curry favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu flattered, schemed, and crawled among the five Hou for favor.

sentences.zh: 是以硃雲抗節求尚方斬馬劍，欲以斬禹，以戒其餘，可謂忠矣。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhu Yun withstood integrity seeking the imperial workshop's decapitation sword, wishing to behead Yu to warn the rest—may be called loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yun demanded the horse-cutting sword to behead Zhang Yu as a warning—true loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而成帝尚復不寤，乃以為居下訕上，廷辱保傅，罪死無赦，詔御史將雲下，欲急烹之。

translations.literal: Yet Chengdi still did not wake; then thought it dwelling below and slandering above, court-insulting the tutor—crime deserved death without pardon—ordered the censor to drag Yun down, wishing to boil him in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi called it slander of a tutor and ordered Zhu Yun boiled alive.

sentences.zh: 雲攀殿折檻，幸賴左將軍辛慶忌叩頭流血，以死爭之。

translations.literal: Yun climbed the hall and broke the railing; fortunately relying on General of the Left Xin Qingji knocking head until blood flowed, contending with death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yun broke the palace rail; only General Xin Qingji’s bloody protest saved him.

sentences.zh: 若不然，則雲已摧碎矣。

translations.literal: If not, then Yun would already have been smashed to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Else Zhu Yun would have died at once.

sentences.zh: 後雖釋檻不修，欲以彰明直臣，誠足以為後世之戒，何益於漢室所由亡也哉！

translations.literal: Later though they released the railing unrepaired, wishing to display straight ministers—truly enough to be a later age's warning—what use toward the reason Han house perished!
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the broken rail honored frank speech—but could not save Han from ruin.

sentences.zh: 然世之論者以為亂臣賊子無道之甚者莫過於莽，此亦猶紂之不善不如是之甚也。

translations.literal: Yet worldly debaters hold that among rebellious ministers and wicked sons none lacked the Way worse than Mang—this is also like saying Zhou's evil was not this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Men say no traitor matched Wang Mang—yet Zhou was no worse.

sentences.zh: 傳稱莽始起外戚，折節力行，以要名譽，宗族稱孝，朋友歸仁。

translations.literal: Tradition says Mang first rose as outer-court kin, bent his conduct and practiced austerity to seek reputation; kin called him filial, friends returned to his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Mang began as humble kin, feigned virtue, and won praise as filial and kind.

sentences.zh: 及其輔政成、哀之際，勤勞國家，動見稱述。

translations.literal: When he assisted government between Cheng and Ai, he toiled for the state and was praised whenever he acted.
translations.idiomatic: As regent for Cheng and Ai he seemed diligent and praised.

sentences.zh: 然于時人士詣闕上書薦莽者不可稱紀，內外群臣莫不歸莽功德。

translations.literal: Yet at that time gentlemen going to the palace gate to submit memorials recommending Mang could not be counted in records; inner and outer ministers none did not return to Mang's merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Countless memorials praised him; every minister sang his virtue.

sentences.zh: 遭遇漢室中微，國嗣三絕，而太后壽考，為之宗主，故莽得遂策命孺子而奪其位也。

translations.literal: Meeting Han house mid-decline, the heir thrice cut off, while the empress dowager lived long as clan head—therefore Mang could carry out orders on the child emperor and seize his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Han lacked an heir; the dowager lived on; Mang crowned a child and stole the throne.

sentences.zh: 昔湯、武之興，亦逆取而順守之耳。

translations.literal: Formerly Tang and Wu's rise also took in reverse yet guarded in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu too seized power, then ruled justly.

sentences.zh: 向莽深惟殷、周取守之術，崇道德，務仁義，履信實，去華偽，施惠天下，十有八年，恩足以感百姓，義足以結英雄，人懷其德，豪傑並用，如此，宗廟社稷宜未滅也，光武雖復賢才，大業詎可冀哉！

translations.literal: If Mang had deeply pondered Yin and Zhou's methods of taking and guarding, exalted virtue and duty, practiced trust and truth, removed show and fraud, spread favor over all under Heaven for eighteen years—favor enough to move the hundred surnames, righteousness enough to bind heroes—men cherishing his virtue, heroes all employed—like this, ancestral temples and altars ought not yet to have perished; even if Guangwu again had worthies, how could the great enterprise be hoped!
translations.idiomatic: Had Mang ruled with true benevolence eighteen years, he might have kept the temples; even Guangwu could not have risen.

sentences.zh: 莽即位之後，自謂得天人之助，以為功廣三王，德茂唐、虞，乃自驕矜，奮其威詐，班宣符讖，震暴殘酷，窮凶極惡，人怨神怒，冬雷電以驚其耳目，夏地動以惕其心腹。

translations.literal: After Mang mounted the throne, he thought himself aided by Heaven and men, deemed his merit broader than the three kings and his virtue richer than Tang and Yu—thereupon he grew arrogant, flaunted awe and fraud, promulgated talisman prophecies, shook and cruelly exposed, exhausted utmost evil—men resented and spirits raged—winter thunder and lightning to startle his ears and eyes, summer earth-quakes to warn his heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he thought himself heaven-sent, boasted past the sage-kings, spread omens, ruled with terror, until men and gods raged and omens shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 而莽猶不知覺悟，方復重行不順時之令，竟連伍之刑，佞媚者親幸，忠諫者誅夷。

translations.literal: Yet Mang still did not know to wake; then again heavily enforced untimely orders, even linked-five punishments; flatterers were favored, loyal remonstrators slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Still he doubled harsh laws, rewarded sycophants, and killed the frank.

sentences.zh: 由是天下忿憤，內外俱發，四海分崩，城池不守，身死於匹夫之手，為天下笑，豈不異哉！

translations.literal: Thereupon all under Heaven resented in anger, inner and outer together rose, the four seas split apart, city walls not defended—he died in a common man's hands, laughed at by all under Heaven—is it not strange!
translations.idiomatic: The realm revolted; he died at a commoner’s hands—a laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 其所由然者，非取之過，而守之非道也。

translations.literal: What made it so was not error in seizing but error in guarding.
translations.idiomatic: He fell not from taking power but from misruling it.

sentences.zh: 莽既屠肌，六合雲擾，劉聖公已立而不辨，盆子承之而覆敗，公孫述又稱帝於蜀漢。

translations.literal: After Mang had been butchered, the six directions cloud-disturbed; Liu Shengong was set up yet not distinguished; Penzi succeeded him yet overturned in defeat; Gongsun Shu again styled himself emperor in Shu-Han.
translations.idiomatic: After Mang fell, Liu Xuan, Liu Penzi, and Gongsun Shu each claimed the throne in turn.

sentences.zh: 如此數子，固非所謂應天順人者，徒為光武之驅除者耳。

translations.literal: Such several men were certainly not what is called answering Heaven and following men—merely those who cleared the road for Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: None of them matched Heaven or the people—they only swept the path for Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，蓋亦天下之天下，非一人之天下也。

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven is also all under Heaven's all under Heaven—not one man's all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The empire belongs to the world, not to one man.

sentences.zh: 「殷商之旅，其會如林，矢於牧野，維予侯興。

translations.literal: "The hosts of Yin-Shang, their meeting like a forest, they set arrow at Muye—'It is we, the marquises, who rise.'
translations.idiomatic: As the *Odes* say of Muye, ‘The Yin host stood thick as a wood—yet the lords rose for Zhou.’

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「侯服于周，天命靡常。

translations.literal: " Again it says: "The marquises submit to Zhou; Heaven's mandate is not constant."
translations.idiomatic: And, ‘Lords bow to Zhou—Heaven’s mandate is not fixed.’

sentences.zh: 」由此言之，主非常人也，有德則天下歸之，無德則天下叛之。

translations.literal: " From this speaking, the lord is not a constant person—having virtue then all under Heaven returns to him; lacking virtue then all under Heaven rebels.
translations.idiomatic: So the ruler is no fixed man: virtue wins the realm, vice loses it.

sentences.zh: 故古之明王，其勞心遠慮，常如臨川無津涯。

translations.literal: Therefore ancient enlightened kings labored heart and planned far, always as if facing a river without ford or shore.
translations.idiomatic: Wise kings toiled as if standing on a shoreless river.

sentences.zh: 於是法天地，象四時，隆恩德，敬大臣，近忠直，遠佞人。

translations.literal: Thereupon they modeled Heaven and earth, imitated the four seasons, raised favor and virtue, respected great ministers, drew near loyalty and straightness, kept distance from flatterers.
