translations.idiomatic: They mirrored heaven and earth, honored ministers, drew near the loyal, and spurned flatterers.

sentences.zh: 仁孝著乎宮牆，弘化洽乎兆庶；

translations.literal: Benevolence and filial piety showed within palace walls; great transforming influence harmonized the millions.
translations.idiomatic: Filial kindness filled the palace; their teaching warmed the people.

sentences.zh: 為平直如砥矢，信義感人神。

translations.literal: Acting straight as whetstone and arrow, trust and righteousness moved men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Their justice was straight as a whetstone; their faith moved gods and men.

sentences.zh: 雖有椒房外戚之寵，不受其委曲之言；

translations.literal: Though there was favor for pepper-room outer kin, they did not accept their crooked words.
translations.idiomatic: They heard no crooked whispers from imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 雖有近習愛幸之豎，不聽其姑息之辭。

translations.literal: Though there were attendants loved and favored as eunuchs, they did not listen to their indulgent phrases.
translations.idiomatic: They heeded no wheedling from favorite attendants.

sentences.zh: 四門穆穆，辟而不闔，待諫者而無忌。

translations.literal: The four gates were august, open yet not closed, awaiting remonstrators without taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The four gates stood open; remonstrance was welcome without taboo.

sentences.zh: 恆戰戰慄栗，不忘戒懼，所以欲永終天祿，恐為將來賢 聖之驅除也。

translations.literal: Always trembling in fear, not forgetting caution and fear—therefore wishing to end Heaven's mandate forever, fearing to become a clearing-away for later worthies and sages.
translations.idiomatic: They trembled on the throne, lest they become stepping-stones for a later founder.

sentences.zh: 且臣聞之，懼危者，常安者也；

translations.literal: Moreover your subject has heard: those who fear peril are constantly at peace.
translations.idiomatic: They say he who fears danger stays safe.

sentences.zh: 憂亡者，恆存者也。

translations.literal: Those who worry about perishing are constantly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He who fears ruin survives.

sentences.zh: 使夫有國之君能安不忘危，則本枝百世，長保榮祚，名位與天地無窮，亦何慮乎為來者之驅除哉！

translations.literal: If lords who possess a state can be in peace yet not forget peril, then root and branches a hundred generations, long preserve glory and mandate, name and position without end with Heaven and earth—what worry then of being clearing-away for those who come after!
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler stays vigilant in peace, his line endures—why fear making way for another?

sentences.zh: 傳有之曰：「狂夫之言，明主察焉。」

translations.literal: Tradition has it: "The madman's words—the enlightened ruler examines them."
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says, ‘Even a madman’s words the wise ruler weighs.’

sentences.zh: 其二曰：士之立業，行非一概。

translations.literal: The second says: gentlemen's establishing enterprise—conduct is not of one pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Second: careers differ—conduct is not one mold.

sentences.zh: 吳起貪官，母死不歸，殺妻求將，不孝之甚。

translations.literal: Wu Qi was greedy for office, on mother's death did not return, killed his wife to seek generalship—unfilial in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qi chased office, skipped his mother’s funeral, killed his wife for a command—deeply unfilial.

sentences.zh: 然在魏，使秦人不敢東向；

translations.literal: Yet in Wei he made Qin men not dare face east.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Wei he froze Qin’s eastward gaze.

sentences.zh: 在楚，則三晉不敢南謀。

translations.literal: In Chu then the three Jin did not dare plot south.
translations.idiomatic: In Chu he checked the three Jin to the north.

sentences.zh: 曾參、閔騫，誠孝子也，不能宿夕離其親，豈肯出身致死，涉危險之地哉！

translations.literal: Zeng Shen and Min Qian were truly filial sons—they could not overnight leave their kin—how could they be willing to leave body and risk death, tread perilous ground!
translations.idiomatic: Zeng and Min would not leave their parents a night—unlike warriors who rush to danger.

sentences.zh: 今大晉應期運之所授，齊聖美于有虞，而吳人不臣，稱帝私附，此亦國之羞也。

translations.literal: Now great Jin receives what fate and season confer, matches sagely beauty to Yu Shun, yet Wu men do not submit as ministers, privately attach and style emperor—this too is the state's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin rivals sage Yao, yet Wu still styles itself emperor—a shame to us.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠欲致熊羆之士，不二心之臣，使奮威淮浦、震服蠻荊者，故宜疇咨博采，廣開貢士之路，薦岩穴，舉賢才，征命考試，匪俊莫用。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to draw bear-and-paw men and ministers of single heart, make them shake awe on the Huai shore and awe the Man and Jing—then you ought to consult widely and broadly open the road of tribute scholars, recommend cave recluses, raise worthies, summon and examine—none but the outstanding employed.
translations.idiomatic: To win heroes for the Huai front, open every path to talent, search hills and halls, test and hire only the best.

sentences.zh: 今台閣選舉，塗塞耳目，九品訪人，唯問中正。

translations.literal: Now terrace and pavilion selection blocks ears and eyes; the nine-rank inquiry asks only the grand rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Today bureaus pick men blindfolded; the nine-rank system asks only the rectifier.

sentences.zh: 故據上品者，非公侯之子孫，則當塗之昆弟也。

translations.literal: Therefore those who hold upper rank are not duke and marquis grandsons then men of power's brothers.
translations.idiomatic: So high ranks go to sons of lords or brothers of the mighty.

sentences.zh: 二者苟然，則蓽門蓬戶之俊，安得不有陸沈者哉！

translations.literal: If both are thus, then how can thatch-gate hovel's excellence not have men sunk in oblivion!
translations.idiomatic: Then talent born in hovels is buried unseen.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：昔田子方養老馬，而窮士知所歸，況居天下之廣居，立天下之正位，行天下之大道乎！

translations.literal: The third says: Formerly Tian Zifang kept old horses and poor shi knew where to return—how much more dwelling in all under Heaven's broad dwelling, standing in all under Heaven's correct position, walking all under Heaven's great road!
translations.idiomatic: Third: Tian Zifang’s care for old horses drew poor scholars; how much more should a Son of Heaven live the great life of the classics.

sentences.zh: 昔明王聖主，無不養老。

translations.literal: Formerly enlightened kings and sage lords none failed to nurture the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Every sage king fed the old.

sentences.zh: 老人眾多，未必皆賢，不可悉養。

translations.literal: The old are many—not necessarily all worthy; cannot all be nurtured.
translations.idiomatic: Many elderly are not sages—you cannot feed every one.

sentences.zh: 故父事三老，所以明孝；

translations.literal: Therefore they served the three elders as fathers to make clear filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: So the throne honored three elders as fathers to teach filial piety.

sentences.zh: 宗事五更，所以明敬。

translations.literal: They honored the five elders to make clear respect.
translations.idiomatic: It honored five elders to teach reverence.

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「吾老以及人之老，吾幼以及人之幼。

translations.literal: Mencius said: "I extend old age to others' old, I extend young to others' young.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, ‘Treat the aged of others as you treat your own.’

sentences.zh: 」今天下雖定，而華山之陽無放馬之群，桃林之下未有休息之牛，故以吳人尚未臣服故也。

translations.literal: " Now though all under Heaven is settled, yet south of Mount Hua there is no herd of resting horses, below Peach Forest no resting ox—because Wu men have not yet submitted as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Peace is declared, yet no horses graze south of Mount Hua—because Wu still defies us.

sentences.zh: 夫饑者易為食，渴者易為飲，天下元元瞻望新政。

translations.literal: The hungry are easily fed, the thirsty easily given drink—all under Heaven's common folk gaze hoping at new government.
translations.idiomatic: Hungry men swallow any food; the people hunger for your new rule.

sentences.zh: 願陛下思子方之仁，念犬馬之勞，思帷蓋之報，發仁惠之詔，廣開養老之制。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to ponder Zifang's benevolence, recall dog-and-horse's toil, think curtain-and-cover repayment, issue benevolent and gracious edicts, broadly open systems for nurturing the aged.
translations.idiomatic: Ponder Tian Zifang’s kindness, remember old servants, repay past favors, and proclaim a generous code for the aged.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：法令賞罰，莫大乎信。

translations.literal: The fourth says: in laws, orders, rewards, and punishments nothing is greater than trust.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: in law and reward nothing tops trust.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：「人而無信，不知其可。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: "A man without trust—how can he stand."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, ‘Without trust a man is nothing.’

sentences.zh: 」況有養人以惠，使人以義，而可以不信行之哉！

translations.literal: " How much more nurturing men with favor, employing men with righteousness—yet can one practice it without trust!
translations.idiomatic: How then nurture men with kindness or duty without keeping faith?

sentences.zh: 臣前為西郡太守，被州所下《己未詔書》：「羌胡道遠，其但募取樂行，不樂勿強。

translations.literal: Your subject formerly was prefect of the western commandery, received from the province the Jiawei edict text: "Qiang and Hu roads are distant—only recruit those glad to go; those not glad, do not force.
translations.idiomatic: As western prefect I received the jiwei edict: ‘Recruit Qiang and Hu only if willing—never force.’

sentences.zh: 」臣被詔書，輒宣恩廣募，示以賞信，所得人名即條言征西。

translations.literal: " Your subject received the edict text, then spread favor and broadly recruited, showed them reward and trust; obtained persons' names then itemized and reported to the general who pacifies the west.
translations.idiomatic: I published the edict, promised pay, and listed every volunteer for the western command.

sentences.zh: 其晉人自可差簡丁強，如法調取；

translations.literal: As for Jin people, themselves can be dispatched and selected for stalwart able-bodied, according to law levied and taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jin subjects may be drafted by the usual rules.

sentences.zh: 至於羌胡，非恩意告諭，則無欲度金城、河西者也。

translations.literal: As for Qiang and Hu, unless by favor's intent proclaimed and instructed, then they have no wish to cross Jincheng and west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang and Hu will not cross the Long frontier unless persuaded with kindness and pay.

sentences.zh: 自往每興軍渡河，未曾有變，故刺史郭綏勸帥有方，深加獎厲，要許重報。

translations.literal: From the past whenever raising army and crossing the river, there has never been change—therefore prefect Guo Sui encouraged and led with method, deeply added rewards and spurs, promised heavy repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Past river campaigns stayed calm; Prefect Guo Sui led well and promised rich reward.

sentences.zh: 是以所募感恩利賞，遂立績效，功在第一。

translations.literal: Therefore those recruited felt gratitude for profit and reward, thereupon set up merit and effect, merit in first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Volunteers trusted the pay and won first-class merit.

sentences.zh: 今州郡督將，並已受封，羌胡健兒，或王或侯，不蒙論敘也。

translations.literal: Now province and commandery commanders all have received enfeoffment; Qiang and Hu stalwarts, some kings or marquises, do not receive narrative of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now commanders are enfeoffed while Qiang and Hu heroes—even kings and marquises among them—go unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 晉文猶不貪原而失信，齊桓不惜地而背盟，況聖主乎！

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin still did not begrudge Yuan and break trust; Duke Huan of Qi did not spare land and betray covenant—how much more a sage lord!
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen would not break faith for land; Duke Huan kept his word—how much more should a sage emperor!

sentences.zh: 其五曰：昔周、漢之興，樹親建德，周因五等之爵，漢有河山之誓。

translations.literal: The fifth says: Formerly Zhou and Han's rise planted kin and established virtue; Zhou relied on five-grade nobles, Han had oath on rivers and mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: Zhou and Han enfeoffed kin—Zhou with five ranks, Han with iron oaths.

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，神器奪於重臣，國祚移於他人。

translations.literal: When they declined, the divine vessel was seized by weighty ministers, state mandate shifted to others.
translations.idiomatic: When they fell, great ministers seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 故滅周者秦，非姬姓也；

translations.literal: Therefore what destroyed Zhou was Qin—not the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ended Zhou, not a Ji prince.

sentences.zh: 代漢者魏，非劉氏也。

translations.literal: What replaced Han was Wei—not the Liu surname.
translations.idiomatic: Wei replaced Han, not a Liu.

sentences.zh: 於今國家大計，使異姓無裂土專封之邑，同姓並據有連城之地，縱復令諸王後世子孫還自相並，蓋亦楚人失繁弱於雲夢，尚未為亡其弓也。

translations.literal: As for today's great state plan, making different surnames lack fiefs that split soil and monopolize enfeoffment, while same surname together occupy lands of linked cities—even if later you let the various princes' posterity and grandsons return to mutually annexing each other, it is also like Chu men losing Fanruo at Yunmeng—not yet having lost their bow.
translations.idiomatic: Let kin hold linked cities while outsiders hold no great fiefs; even if princes later fight among themselves, the imperial regalia stays in the family—like losing one bow in Yunmeng yet keeping the rest.

sentences.zh: 其於神器不移他族，則始祖不遷之廟，萬年億兆不改其名矣。

translations.literal: As for the divine vessel not shifting to other clans, then the founder's unmoved temple, myriad years and hundred million not changing its name.
translations.idiomatic: So long as the throne stays in the clan, the founder’s temple stands unmoved for ages.

sentences.zh: 大晉諸王二十餘人，而公侯伯子男五百餘國，欲言其國皆小乎，則漢祖之起，俱無尺土之地，況有國者哉！

translations.literal: Great Jin's princes are over twenty, while dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons exceed five hundred states—if you say their states are all small, then Han Gaozu's rise together lacked a foot of soil—how much more those who possess states!
translations.idiomatic: Jin has twenty princes and five hundred petty lords—yet Han’s founder began landless; size is no excuse.

sentences.zh: 將謂大晉世世賢聖，而諸侯之胤常不肖邪，則放勳欽明而有丹硃，瞽瞍頑凶面虞舜。

translations.literal: Will you say great Jin generation after generation is all sage worthy, while feudal lords' descendants are always unworthy—then Fangxun was enlightened yet had Dan Zhu; Gu Sou was stubbornly vicious yet had Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Sage emperors bore foolish sons; wicked fathers sired Shun—blood alone guarantees nothing.

sentences.zh: 天下有事無不由兵，而無故多樹兵本，廣開亂原，臣故曰五等不便也。

translations.literal: All under Heaven has affairs none not from arms—yet without cause many times planting the root of arms, broadly opening the source of chaos—your subject therefore says the five grades are not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Every crisis calls arms—yet multiplying armies and nobles only breeds chaos; the five ranks are a bad tool.

sentences.zh: 臣以為可如前表，諸王宜大其國，增益其兵，悉遣守籓，使形勢足以相接，則陛下可高枕而臥耳。

translations.literal: Your subject holds one may as in the former memorial: the various princes ought to enlarge their states, increase their troops, all dispatch them to guard fiefs, so that terrain and strength suffice to link—then Your Majesty can pillow high and sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Enlarge princely domains, give them troops, send them to their fiefs with strength to support one another—then you may sleep soundly.

sentences.zh: 臣以為諸侯伯子男名號皆宜改易之，使封爵之制，祿奉禮秩，並同天下諸侯之例。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that feudal lords', earls', viscounts', and barons' titles all ought to be changed and altered, making enfeoffment's system, stipend salary ritual rank, together match all under Heaven's feudal lords' precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Rename the petty ranks and align their stipends with true feudal precedent.

sentences.zh: 臣聞與覆車同軌者未嘗安也，與死人同病者未嘗生也，與亡國同法者未嘗存也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that those who share a rut with an overturned cart have never been secure; those who share sickness with the dead have never lived; those who share law with a perished state have never survived.
translations.idiomatic: He who rides the same track as a wreck, shares the corpse’s fever, or copies a dead law will not endure.

sentences.zh: 況夫巍巍大晉，方將登太山，禪梁父，刻石書勳，垂示無窮。

translations.literal: How much more towering great Jin, about to ascend Mount Tai, perform Liangfu feng, carve stone and write merit, hang display without end.
translations.idiomatic: How much more should mighty Jin, ready to claim heaven’s mandate, learn from history and guard the deed you carve in stone.

sentences.zh: 宜遠鑒往代興廢，深為嚴防，使著事奮筆，必有紀焉。

translations.literal: Ought far to mirror former generations' rise and fall, deeply make strict guard, so that when writers take brush there must be record.
translations.idiomatic: Look far at rise and fall so future scribes have a clear record.

sentences.zh: 昔伊尹恥其君不為堯、舜，此臣所以私懷慷慨，自忘輕賤者也。

translations.literal: Formerly Yi Yin was ashamed his lord was not Yao and Shun—this is why your subject privately harbors generous ardor, forgetting his lightness and baseness.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin shamed his king into virtue—that is why I speak bluntly despite my low rank.

sentences.zh: 灼書奏，帝覽而異焉，擢為明威將軍、魏興太守。

translations.literal: When Zhuo's book was submitted, the emperor read and marveled, promoted him to general who displays awesomeness and prefect of Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read his memorial with wonder and made him general who displays might and prefect of Weixing.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 閻纘，字續伯，巴西安漢人也。

translations.literal: Yan Zuan, style Xubo, was a man of Anhan in Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan, courtesy name Xubo, came from Anhan in Baxi.

sentences.zh: 祖圃，為張魯功曹，勸魯降魏，封平樂鄉侯。

translations.literal: Grandfather Pu was Zhang Lu's workhouse clerk, urged Lu to surrender Wei, was enfeoffed village marquis of Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan Pu was Zhang Lu’s clerk, urged surrender to Wei, and was enfeoffed as village marquis of Pingle.

sentences.zh: 父璞，嗣爵，仕吳至牂柯太守。

translations.literal: His father Pu inherited the noble rank, served Wu up to prefect of Zangke.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan Pu inherited the title and rose to prefect of Zangke under Wu.

sentences.zh: 纘僑居河南新安，少游英豪，多所交結，博覽墳典，該通物理。

translations.literal: Zuan sojourned in Xin'an in Henan, in youth roamed heroes, broadly formed ties, widely read the tombs' canons, thoroughly comprehended things' pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan lived in Xin’an, befriended bold spirits in youth, read widely, and mastered practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 父卒，繼母不慈，纘恭事彌謹。

translations.literal: When father died, the stepmother was not kind; Zuan served her with respect ever more careful.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died his stepmother was cruel, yet he served her with growing reverence.

sentences.zh: 而母疾之愈甚，乃誣纘盜父時金寶，訟於有司。

translations.literal: Yet the mother hated him ever more, then slandered Zuan stealing father's time gold and jewels, sued at the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: She hated him more, accused him of stealing his father’s gold, and hauled him to court.

sentences.zh: 遂被清議十餘年，纘無怨色，孝謹不怠。

translations.literal: Thereupon he suffered pure discussion over ten years; Zuan had no resentful look, filial care not slack.
translations.idiomatic: Pure opinion ostracized him for years; he showed no bitterness and kept filial duty.

sentences.zh: 母后意解，更移中正，乃得復品。

translations.literal: Later the mother's mind relented, again shifted the grand rectifier, then was able to regain grading.
translations.idiomatic: When her heart softened and the rectifier was changed, his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 為太傅楊駿舍人，轉安復令。

translations.literal: He became attendant to grand tutor Yang Jun, transferred to magistrate of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: He served Yang Jun as attendant, then became magistrate of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 駿之誅也，纘棄官歸，要駿故主簿潘岳、掾崔基等共葬之。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, Zuan cast aside office and returned, invited Jun's former chief clerk Pan Yue and aide Cui Ji and others jointly to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun fell, Yan Zuan quit office, rallied Pan Yue, Cui Ji, and others to bury him.

sentences.zh: 基、嶽畏罪，推纘為主。

translations.literal: Ji and Yue feared guilt, pushed Zuan as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Cui and Pan, fearing punishment, made Yan Zuan lead the burial.

sentences.zh: 墓成，當葬，駿從弟模告武陵王澹，將表殺造意者。

translations.literal: When the tomb was finished, about to bury, Jun's cousin Mo reported to Prince Wuling, Dan, intending to memorialize killing the originators.
translations.idiomatic: When the tomb was ready, Yang Mo told Prince Wuling of a plan to execute the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 眾咸懼，填塚而逃，纘獨以家財成墓，葬駿而去。

translations.literal: All were afraid, filled the mound and fled; Zuan alone used family wealth to complete the tomb, buried Jun, then left.
translations.idiomatic: The others fled; Yan Zuan spent his own fortune to finish the tomb and bury Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒鄒湛以纘才堪佐著作，薦于秘書監華嶠。

translations.literal: Libationer of the imperial academy Zou Zhen held that Zuan's talent sufficed to assist editorial work, recommended him to overseer of the secretariat Hua Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhen recommended him to Hua Qiao for the editorial office.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「此職閑廩重，貴勢多爭之，不暇求其才。

translations.literal: Qiao said: "This post is idle yet salary heavy; noble power many fight for it—no leisure to seek his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiao said the post was a sinceure that great families fought over—no room to judge talent.

sentences.zh: 」遂不能用。

translations.literal: " Thereupon could not use.
translations.idiomatic: So he was not hired.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒引為西戎校尉司馬，有功，封平樂鄉侯。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian, Yong, drew him in as marshal to the colonel of the western Rong, had merit, enfeoffed village marquis of Pingle.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hejian Sima Yong made him marshal on the western frontier; he earned the Pingle village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子之廢也，纘輿棺詣闕，上書理太子之冤曰：

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai was deposed, Zuan carried a coffin to the palace gate, submitted a memorial setting right the crown prince's wrong, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Sima Yu was deposed, Yan Zuan carried a coffin to the gate and begged justice in a memorial:

sentences.zh: 伏見赦文及榜下前太子遹手疏，以為驚愕。

translations.literal: Prostrate I saw the amnesty text and the former crown prince Yu's hand draft posted below—I thought it shocking.
translations.idiomatic: I read the amnesty and the former heir’s own writing with shock.

sentences.zh: 自古以來，臣子悖逆，未有如此之甚也。

translations.literal: From antiquity minister and son rebellion has never been this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Never has a subject’s treason sounded so extreme.

sentences.zh: 幸賴天慈，全其首領。

translations.literal: Fortunately relying on Heaven's kindness, his head and neck were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Mercifully his life was spared.

sentences.zh: 臣伏念遹生於聖父而至此者，由於長養深宮，沈淪富貴，受饒先帝，父母驕之。

translations.literal: Your subject prostrate thinks: Yu was born of a sage father yet reached this—from being reared deep in the palace, sinking in wealth and honor, receiving indulgence from the late emperor, parents doting on him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yu was a sage’s son yet fell so low because he was raised in luxury, spoiled by two emperors.

sentences.zh: 每見選師傅下至群吏，率取膏粱擊鐘鼎食之家，稀有寒門儒素如衛綰、周文、石奮、疏廣，洗馬、舍人亦無汲黯、鄭莊之比，遂使不見事父事君之道。

translations.literal: Whenever I see selection of tutors down to petty clerks, generally they take fat-fed bell-and-tripod households—rarely poor-gate Confucians like Wei Wan, Zhou Wen, Shi Fen, Shu Guang; even tutor and attendant lack Ji An or Zheng Zhuang's match—therefore he never saw the way to serve father or lord.
translations.idiomatic: His tutors were rich drones, not poor scholars like Wei Wan; even his attendants were no Ji An—so he never learned to serve father or ruler.

sentences.zh: 臣案古典，太子居以士禮，與國人齒，以此明先王欲令知先賤然後乃貴。

translations.literal: Your subject checks ancient models: the crown prince dwells by gentleman's ritual, ranks with common folk—by this former kings meant him to know first lowliness then honor.
translations.idiomatic: The classics seat the heir among commoners so he knows humility before honor.

sentences.zh: 自頃東宮亦微太盛，所以致敗也。

translations.literal: Recently the eastern palace was also somewhat too grand—this is what brought defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the heir’s court grew too grand—that invited ruin.

sentences.zh: 非但東宮，曆觀諸王師友文學，皆豪族力能得者，率非龔遂、王陽，能以道訓。

translations.literal: Not only the eastern palace—surveying princes' friends and literary aides, all are what powerful clans can obtain—generally not Gong Sui or Wang Yang able to instruct by the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Princes’ tutors are picked for power, not men like Gong Sui who teach the Way.

sentences.zh: 友無亮直三益之節，官以文學為名，實不讀書，但共鮮衣好馬，縱酒高會，嬉遊博弈，豈有切磋，能相長益！

translations.literal: Friends lack the three-excellences' straightness; offices titled 'literary' in fact do not read books—only share fine clothes and good horses, heavy drinking and high feasts, sport and gambling—how could there be grinding that mutually lengthens and benefits!
translations.idiomatic: Friends lack the three good companions; ‘literary’ aides never read—only race horses and gamble.

sentences.zh: 臣常恐公族遲陵，以此歎息。

translations.literal: Your subject always feared the ducal clans' decline—therefore sighed.
translations.idiomatic: I have long feared for the imperial kin and sighed.

sentences.zh: 今遹可以為戒，恐其被斥，棄逐遠郊，始當悔過，無所復及。

translations.literal: Now Yu can be a warning; I fear once he is cast out to distant suburbs he will repent with no way back.
translations.idiomatic: Let Yu be a warning—if you banish him too far he may repent too late.

sentences.zh: 昔戾太子無狀，稱兵距命，而壺關三老上書，有田千秋之言，猶曰：「子弄父兵，罪應笞耳！

translations.literal: Formerly crown prince Li lacked deportment, raised arms and resisted orders—yet Huguan's three elders submitted a memorial, having Tian Qianqiu's words—still saying 'the son wielded father's arms—crime should be flogging!'
translations.idiomatic: Even Han’s rebel Heir Li was excused as a boy’s folly when elders spoke.

sentences.zh: 」漢武感悟之，築思子之台。

translations.literal: " Han Wu was moved and built the Son-Reflecting terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Wu built the Terrace of Longing for a Son.

sentences.zh: 今遹無狀，言語悖逆，受罪之日，不敢失道，猶為輕于戾太子，尚可禁持，重選保傅。

translations.literal: Now Yu lacks deportment, words rebellious—on the day of receiving punishment he did not lose the Way—still lighter than crown prince Li—still can be restrained, heavily reselect tutors and protectors.
translations.idiomatic: Yu’s fault is lighter than Prince Li’s; choose new tutors and he may yet be saved.

sentences.zh: 如司空張華，道德深遠，乃心忠誠，以為之師。

translations.literal: Such as Minister of Works Zhang Hua, deep in virtue and far in the Way, heart loyal—make him tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Name Zhang Hua tutor—his virtue is deep and his loyalty sure.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫劉寔，寒苦自立，終始不衰，年同呂望，經藉不廢，以為之保。

translations.literal: Grand Counsellor Liu Shi, poor and self-established, never slackening, age matching Lü Wang, classics not abandoned—make him protector.
translations.idiomatic: Name Liu Shi protector—poor, upright, and learned as Lü Wang in old age.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射裴頠，明允恭肅，體道居正，以為之友。

translations.literal: Vice-director Pei Wei, bright, trustworthy, reverent, embodying the Way and dwelling correct—make him friend.
translations.idiomatic: Name Pei Wei friend—he is clear-minded and upright.

sentences.zh: 置游談文學，皆選寒門孤宦以學行自立者，及取服勤更事、涉履艱難、事君事親、名行素聞者，使與共處。

translations.literal: Set roaming-talk literary aides—all select poor-gate orphaned officials who by learning and conduct self-establish, also take those who toiled in office, trod hardship, served lord and kin with heard-of name and conduct—make them dwell together.
translations.idiomatic: Fill his staff with poor scholars of proven conduct who know hardship.

sentences.zh: 使嚴御史監護其家，絕貴戚子弟、輕薄賓客。

translations.literal: Order stern censors to guard his household, cutting off noble sons and flighty guests.
translations.idiomatic: Post stern censors to bar noble idlers from his gate.

sentences.zh: 如此，左右前後，莫非正人。

translations.literal: Like this, left and right, before and behind, none are not upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Then every face around him will be upright.

sentences.zh: 師傅文學，可令十日一講，使共論議於前。

translations.literal: Tutors and literary aides—order once every ten days one lecture, make them debate before him.
translations.idiomatic: Have tutors lecture every ten days and debate before the heir.

sentences.zh: 敕使但道古今孝子慈親，忠臣事君，及思愆改過之義，皆聞善道，庶幾可全。

translations.literal: Order them only to speak of ancient filial sons, loyal ministers serving lords, and thinking faults to change—let all hear the good way—perhaps he can be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Let them teach filial piety, loyalty, and repentance until he hears only good.

sentences.zh: 昔太甲有罪，放之三年，思庸克復，為殷明王。

translations.literal: Formerly Taijia had guilt, was banished three years, thought on common duty and could return—became Yin's enlightened king.
translations.idiomatic: Taijia was banished, repented, and became a good king.

sentences.zh: 又魏文帝懼於見廢，夙夜自祗，竟能自全。

translations.literal: Again Wei Wendi feared being deposed, day and night self-warned, in the end could preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wendi feared deposition and saved himself by caution.

sentences.zh: 及至明帝，因母得罪，廢為平原侯，為置家臣庶子，師友文學，皆取正人，共相匡矯。

translations.literal: Down to Mingdi, because mother offended, was deposed as marquis of Pingyuan—for him were set household ministers, sons, tutors, and literary aides, all taking upright men, together correcting.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi, deposed as a prince, was surrounded by upright tutors who corrected him.

sentences.zh: 兢兢慎罰，事父以孝，父沒，事母以謹，聞于天下，於今稱之。

translations.literal: Fearful and careful in punishments, serving father with filial piety; father gone, serving mother with care—heard of all under Heaven, to this day they praise him.
translations.idiomatic: He grew filial and careful and is praised to this day.

sentences.zh: 漢高皇帝數置酒於庭，欲廢太子，後四皓為師，子房為傅，竟復成就。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu several times set wine in the court, wished to depose the crown prince—later the four hoary elders became tutors, Zifang became protector—at last again was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu nearly replaced the heir until the Four Elders and Zhang Liang saved him.

sentences.zh: 前事不忘，後事之戒。

translations.literal: Not forgetting former affairs is later affairs' warning.
translations.idiomatic: Past deeds are warnings for the future.

sentences.zh: 孟軻有雲，「孤臣孽子，其操心也危，慮患也深」，故多善功。

translations.literal: Mencius said, 'The orphaned minister and concubine's son—their care is perilous, their worry deep'—therefore many good deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said peril breeds virtue in the disinherited.

sentences.zh: 李斯云：「慈母多敗子，嚴家無格虜。

translations.literal: Li Si said: 'A doting mother many defeated sons; a strict house has no shackled captives.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si said indulgent mothers ruin sons and strict homes breed no slaves.

sentences.zh: 」由陛下驕遹使至於此，庶其受罪以來，足自思改。

translations.literal: " From Your Majesty's doting on Yu he reached this; perhaps since receiving punishment it is enough to think and change.
translations.idiomatic: Your doting brought him here; punishment may teach him to change.

sentences.zh: 方今天下多虞，四夷未寧，將伺國隙。

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven has many worries, four barbarians not quiet, about to watch the state's cracks.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is troubled and barbarians watch for weakness.

sentences.zh: 儲副大事，不宜空虛。

translations.literal: Heir-apparent's great matter ought not be empty.
translations.idiomatic: The succession must not stand vacant.

sentences.zh: 宜為大計，小復停留。

translations.literal: Ought to be great plan, small again delay.
translations.idiomatic: Plan for the throne and delay a little.

sentences.zh: 先加嚴誨。

translations.literal: First add stern instruction.
translations.idiomatic: First lecture him sternly.

sentences.zh: 依平原侯故事，若不悛改，棄之未晚也。

translations.literal: According to the marquis of Pingyuan precedent—if he will not reform, casting him aside is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Wei Mingdi’s example; if he will not mend, depose him later.

sentences.zh: 臣素寒門，無力仕宦，不經東宮，情不私遹。

translations.literal: Your subject by nature is cold gate, without strength to serve in office, has not passed through eastern palace—feeling not private to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: I am a humble outsider with no private tie to the heir.

sentences.zh: 念昔楚國處女諫其王曰「有龍無尾」，言年四十，未有太子。

translations.literal: Thinking formerly Chu state's virgin remonstrated her king saying 'there is a dragon without tail'—meaning age forty yet no crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: A Chu maiden warned of a ‘dragon without tail’—no heir at forty.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗備近職，雖未得自結天日，情同閽寺，悾悾之誠，皆為國計。

translations.literal: Your subject once filled a nearby post, though not able personally to tie to Heaven's sun, feeling same as gatekeeper—earnest sincerity all for state plan.
translations.idiomatic: I served near the throne; though low as a gate guard my heart is for the state.

sentences.zh: 臣老母見臣為表，乃為臣卜卦，云「書禦即死」。

translations.literal: Your subject's old mother saw your subject making a memorial, then for your subject divined, saying 'when the writing reaches the throne, death.'
translations.idiomatic: My mother divined that presenting this memorial would mean my death.

sentences.zh: 妻子守臣，涕泣見止。

translations.literal: Wife and children guarded your subject, weeping and begging stop.
translations.idiomatic: My wife and children begged me with tears to stop.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為頻見拔擢，嘗為近職，此恩難忘，何以報德？

translations.literal: Your subject alone thought: repeatedly seeing promotion, once filling nearby post—this favor hard to forget—how repay virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Yet frequent promotion bound me—how repay such grace?

sentences.zh: 唯當陳誠，以死獻忠。

translations.literal: Only ought to state sincerity, with death offer loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I can only speak my heart even at cost of life.

sentences.zh: 輒具棺絮，伏須刑誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon prepared coffin and shroud, prostrate awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: I brought a coffin and await execution.

sentences.zh: 書禦不省。

translations.literal: The writing reached the throne and was not examined.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 及張華遇害，賈謐被誅，朝野震悚，纘獨撫華屍慟哭曰：「早語君遜位而不肯，今果不免，命也夫！

translations.literal: When Zhang Hua met harm and Jia Mi was executed, court and countryside trembled; Zuan alone stroked Hua's corpse and wept greatly, saying: "Early I told you lord to yield place yet you would not—now indeed could not escape—fate!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua died and Jia Mi fell, Yan Zuan alone wept over Zhang Hua, crying that he had refused to retire in time.

sentences.zh: 」過叱賈謐屍曰：「小兒亂國之由，誅其晚矣！」

translations.literal: " Passing he scolded Jia Mi's corpse: "Little boy source of state's disorder—killing him was late!"
translations.idiomatic: He cursed Jia Mi’s corpse as the boy who ruined the state.

sentences.zh: 皇太孫立，纘復上疏曰：

translations.literal: When imperial great-grandson was set up, Zuan again submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial great-grandson was named heir, Yan Zuan wrote again:

sentences.zh: 臣前上書訟太子之枉，不見省覽。

translations.literal: Your subject earlier submitted a memorial suing the crown prince's wrong—not seen or examined.
translations.idiomatic: My plea for the deposed heir went unread.

sentences.zh: 昔壺關三老陳衛太子之冤，而漢武築思子之台。

translations.literal: Formerly Huguan's three elders stated Wei crown prince's wrong, and Han Wu built Son-Reflecting terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Huguan elders moved Han Wu to build the Terrace of Longing.

sentences.zh: 高廟令田千秋上書，不敢正言，托以鬼神之教，而孝武大感，月中三遷，位至丞相，乘車入殿，號曰車氏。

translations.literal: Gaomiao commandant Tian Qianqiu submitted a memorial, not daring straight speech, entrusting to ghost-god instruction—yet Xiaowu was greatly moved, thrice promoted within a month to chancellor, rode carriage into hall, styled Carriage clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Qianqiu used a riddle yet rose to chancellor in a month.

sentences.zh: 恨臣精誠微薄，不能有感，竟使太子流離，沒命許昌。

translations.literal: I hate that my sincerity was too thin to move you—yet the heir wandered and lost life at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: My feeble words failed; the prince died at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 向令陛下即納臣言，不致此禍。

translations.literal: If only Your Majesty had taken my counsel then, this disaster would not have arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Had you listened, that tragedy would not have happened.

sentences.zh: 天贊聖意，三公獻謀，庶人賜死，罪人斯得，太子以明，臣恨其晚，無所復及。

translations.literal: Heaven aided sagely intent, three dukes offered plan, commoner granted death, criminals thereby obtained—crown prince thereby clarified; your subject hates it was late, nothing again to reach.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven helped: the plotters died and the heir’s innocence emerged—too late for me to help.

sentences.zh: 詔書慈悼，迎喪反葬，復其禮秩，誠副眾望，不意呂、霍之變復生於今日！

translations.literal: Edict kind and mournful, welcoming the bier to return burial, restoring his ritual rank—truly matched the multitude's hope—did not expect Lü and Huo's change again born today!
translations.idiomatic: You recalled the prince’s body and restored his rites—yet I fear another Lü–Huo coup.

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書建立太孫，斯誠陛下上順先典以安社稷，中慰慈悼冤魂之痛，下令萬國心有所系。

translations.literal: Prostrate I saw edict establishing great-grandson—this truly is Your Majesty above following former canons to settle altars, within comforting kind mournful wronged ghost's pain, below ordering myriad regions' hearts to have something to tie to.
translations.idiomatic: Naming the great-grandson heir follows the classics, consoles the dead prince, and steadies the realm.

sentences.zh: 追惟庶人，所為無狀，幾傾宗廟，賴相國、太宰至忠憤發，潛謀俱斷，奉贊聖意，以成神武。

translations.literal: Tracing the commoner's acts—lacking deportment, almost toppled ancestral temples—relying on minister of state and grand tutor utmost loyalty indignant rise, secret plots together cut, assisting sagely intent, to complete divine martial.
translations.idiomatic: The commoner prince nearly ruined the temples until loyal ministers struck down the plot.

sentences.zh: 雖周誅二叔，漢掃諸呂，未足以喻。

translations.literal: Though Zhou executed two uncles, Han swept the Lü—not enough to compare.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhou’s and Han’s purges pale beside it.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下因此大更厘改，以為永制。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty by this greatly to reform and change, taking it as lasting system.
translations.idiomatic: Use this crisis to reform institutions for good.

sentences.zh: 禮置太子，居以士禮，與國人齒，為置官屬，皆如朋友，不為純臣。

translations.literal: Ritual sets crown prince dwelling by gentleman's ritual, ranks with common folk, for him sets official subordinates all like friends, not making pure ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Rite seats the heir among commoners and makes his staff friends, not mere underlings.

sentences.zh: 既使上厭至望，以崇孝道，又令不相嚴憚，易相規正。

translations.literal: Already making above suppress utmost hope to exalt filial way, again making below not mutually fear, easy mutually to regulate and correct.
translations.idiomatic: That satisfies filial awe above and frank counsel below.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武既信奸讒，危害太子，復用望氣之言，欲盡誅詔獄中囚。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Wu already trusted wicked slander, endangered crown prince, again used qi-watcher's words, wished to kill all prisoners in the edict prison.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wu’s slander nearly killed the heir and would have massacred every prisoner on an omen.

sentences.zh: 邴吉以皇孫在焉，閉門距命，後遂擁護皇孫，督罰乳母，卒至成人，立為孝宣皇帝。

translations.literal: Bing Ji because imperial great-grandson was there, closed gate and resisted orders—afterward then embraced and protected great-grandson, supervised and punished wet-nurses—at last reached adulthood, was set up as Emperor Xiaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji barred the gate because the imperial grandson was inside, reared him, and raised Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 苟志於忠，無往不可。

translations.literal: If the will aims at loyalty, nowhere cannot go.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal hearts find a way.

sentences.zh: 曆觀古人雖不避死，亦由世教寬以成節。

translations.literal: Surveying ancients, though they did not avoid death, also from generation's teaching being lenient thereby completed integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient loyalty flourished where law was lenient.

sentences.zh: 吉雖距詔書，事在於忠，故宥而不責。

translations.literal: Though Ji resisted edict text, the matter lay in loyalty—therefore was pardoned and not blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji defied an edict yet was pardoned for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自晉興已來，用法太嚴，遲速之間，輒加誅斬。

translations.literal: Since Jin rose, using law too strict, between slow and fast always added beheading.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin arose the laws have grown cruel—delay means death.

sentences.zh: 一身伏法，猶可強為，今世之誅，動輒滅門。

translations.literal: One body submitting to law still can be forced; today's executions move to exterminating whole clans.
translations.idiomatic: One man might accept death, but Jin wipes out whole clans.

sentences.zh: 昔呂後臨朝，肆意無道。

translations.literal: Formerly Empress Lü faced court, wanton without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü ruled lawlessly.

sentences.zh: 周昌相趙，三召其王而昌不遣，先征昌入，乃後召王。

translations.literal: Zhou Chang chancellor of Zhao—thrice summoned his king yet Chang would not send; first summoned Chang in, only afterward summoned king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chang thrice refused to send the Zhao king until he himself was called to court.

sentences.zh: 此由漢制本寬，得使為快。

translations.literal: This came from Han law originally lenient, could make it swift.
translations.idiomatic: Han law was loose enough to allow that.

sentences.zh: 假令如今，呂後必謂昌已反，夷其三族，則誰敢復為殺身成義者哉！

translations.literal: Suppose like today—Empress Lü would surely say Chang already rebelled, exterminate his three clans—then who would again be one who kills body to complete righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s code Lü would have killed Zhou Chang’s three clans—who then would dare die for right?

sentences.zh: 此法宜改，可使經遠。

translations.literal: This law ought to change—can make it reach far.
translations.idiomatic: Change the law for the long term.

sentences.zh: 又漢初廢趙王張敖，其臣貫高謀弑高祖，高祖不誅，以明臣道。

translations.literal: Again Han at first deposed Zhao king Zhang Ao; his minister Guan Gao plotted to murder Gaozu—Gaozu did not execute, to make clear minister's way.
translations.idiomatic: Han spared Guan Gao to show what ministers owe.

sentences.zh: 田叔、孟舒十人為奴，髡鉗隨王，隱親侍養，故令平安。

translations.literal: Tian Shu, Meng Shu ten men became slaves, shaved and collared following king, hiding kin and serving nurture—therefore ordered peace and safety.
translations.idiomatic: Ten Zhao men shaved their heads as slaves to serve their fallen prince and kept him alive.

sentences.zh: 向使晉法得容為義，東宮之臣得如周昌，固護太子得如邴吉，距詔不坐，伏死諫爭，則聖意必變，太子以安。

translations.literal: Suppose Jin law could tolerate acting for righteousness, eastern palace ministers could be like Zhou Chang, firmly protecting crown prince could be like Bing Ji, resisting edict without sitting crime, lying dead to remonstrate—then sagely intent must change, crown prince thereby safe.
translations.idiomatic: If Jin law honored such loyalty, men like Zhou Chang and Bing Ji could save an heir.

sentences.zh: 如田叔、孟舒侍從不罪者，則隱親左右，奸凶毒藥無緣得設，太子不夭也。

translations.literal: If Tian Shu and Meng Shu's following attendance went unblamed, then hidden kin at left and right, wicked fierce poison no chance to be set—crown prince would not die young.
translations.idiomatic: If attendants like Tian Shu went unpunished, poison could not reach the heir.

sentences.zh: 臣每責東宮臣故無侍從者，後聞頗有于道路望車拜辭，而有司收付洛陽獄，奏科其罪。

translations.literal: Your subject always blamed eastern palace ministers for having no attendants—later heard quite many on roads bowing to carts in farewell, yet authorities seized and delivered to Luoyang prison, memorialized sentencing their crime.
translations.idiomatic: I faulted the heir’s staff for vanishing—then learned many who wept at his cart were jailed.

sentences.zh: 然臣故莫從，良有以也。

translations.literal: Yet your subject for old reason none followed—truly there was cause.
translations.idiomatic: I did not follow him—yet I had good reason.

sentences.zh: 又本置三率，盛其兵馬，所以宿衛防虞。

translations.literal: Again originally setting three rates, making grand their arms and horses—thereby night guard and defense.
translations.idiomatic: The three guard commands were meant to protect the heir.

sentences.zh: 而使者卒至，莫有警嚴覆請審者，此由恐畏滅族。

translations.literal: Yet envoys arrived suddenly, none having alert strictness or double-checked request—this comes from fearing clan extinction.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys came suddenly none dared arm the guard—fearing extermination.

sentences.zh: 今皇孫沖幼，去事多故。

translations.literal: Now imperial great-grandson is young, gone affairs many and strange.
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandson is a child in a time of plots.

sentences.zh: 若有不虞，強臣專制，奸邪矯詐，雖有相國保訓東宮，擁佑之恩同于邴吉，適可使玉體安全，宜開來防，可著於令：自今已後，諸有廢興倉卒，群臣皆得輒嚴，須錄詣殿前，面受口詔，然後為信，得同周昌不遣王節，下聽臣子隱親，得如田叔、孟舒，不加罪責，則永固儲副，以後安嗣之遠慮也。

translations.literal: If there is no preparation, strong ministers monopolize control, wickedness fakes edicts—though there is minister of state protecting and instructing eastern palace, embracing favor's grace same as Bing Ji—only enough to make jade body safe—ought to open coming defense, can be written in ordinance: from now after, all sudden deposals and enthronements, host of ministers all may arm on their own, must assemble at hall front, face receive oral edict, then count as trustworthy—may match Zhou Chang not sending king's tally, below hearing ministers and sons hide kin, may be like Tian Shu, Meng Shu, without adding crime and blame—then forever solidify heir-apparent, with later peace for succession's far planning.
translations.idiomatic: Decree that in sudden successions ministers may arm, must hear the edict in person at court—like Zhou Chang holding the tally or Tian Shu serving a fallen prince—so the heir can be saved.

sentences.zh: 來事難知，往事可改。

translations.literal: Coming affairs hard to know; gone affairs can be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The future is dark; past errors can still be mended.

sentences.zh: 臣前每見詹事裴權用心懇惻，舍人秦戢數上疏啟諫；

translations.literal: Your subject formerly each saw household manager Pei Quan use heart earnestly earnest, attendant Qin Ji several times submit memorials opening remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: I saw Pei Quan serve the heir with zeal and Qin Ji remonstrate again and again.

sentences.zh: 而爰倩贈以九列，權有忠意，獨不蒙賞。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan Qian presented him nine columns; Quan had loyal intent alone not receiving reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qian won nine-rank honors while Pei Quan’s loyalty went unrewarded.

sentences.zh: 謂宜依倩為比，以寵其魂。

translations.literal: I say one ought to follow Qian as precedent to honor his ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Reward Pei Quan posthumously as Yuan Qian was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 推尋表疏，如秦戢輩及司隸所奏，諸敢拜辭于道路者，明詔稱揚，使微異於眾，以勸為善，以獎將來也。

translations.literal: Tracing memorials—such as Qi's sort and what the colonel director reported—those who dared bow farewell on roads—bright edict praise them, make them slightly different from the multitude, to encourage doing good, to award what comes after.
translations.idiomatic: Praise men who wept for the heir at the roadside and honor Qin Ji’s petitions to encourage loyalty.

sentences.zh: 纘又陳：

translations.literal: Zuan again presented:
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan added:

sentences.zh: 今相國雖已保傅東宮，保其安危。

translations.literal: Now minister of state though already tutor-protector to eastern palace, protects his safety.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of state guards the heir’s life.

sentences.zh: 至於旦夕訓誨，輔導出入，動靜劬勞，宜選寒苦之士，忠貞清正，老而不衰，如城門校尉梁柳、白衣南安硃沖比者，以為師傅。

translations.literal: As for dawn-and-dusk instruction, guiding in and out, movement stillness toil—ought to select poor bitter shi, loyal chaste clear upright, old yet not decayed, like colonel of the gates Liang Liu, white-robed Zhu Chong of Nan'an such sorts—to make tutors.
translations.idiomatic: Choose poor, loyal veterans like Liang Liu or Zhu Chong for daily tutoring.

sentences.zh: 其侍臣以下文武將吏，且勿復取盛戚豪門子弟，若吳太妃家室及賈、郭之黨。

translations.literal: As for attendant ministers below civil and military generals and clerks—for the moment do not again take prosperous kin great-gate younger kin, such as Grand Consort Wu's household and Jia, Guo's factions.
translations.idiomatic: Stop staffing the heir with Wu, Jia, or Guo relatives.

sentences.zh: 如此之輩，生而富溢，無念修己，率多輕薄浮華，相驅放縱，皆非所補益於吾少主者也。

translations.literal: Such kinds born overflowing rich, without thought of cultivating self, mostly light thin floating ornament, mutually drive unrestraint—not any who benefit our young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Rich noble boys help neither character nor study.

sentences.zh: 皆可擇寒門篤行、學問素士、更履險易、節義足稱者，以備群臣，可輕其禮儀，使與古同，於相切磋為益。

translations.literal: All can select cold-gate steadfast conduct, learning question plain shi, again treading peril and ease, integrity praiseable—to fill the host of ministers; can lighten their ritual etiquette, make same as antiquity, with mutual grinding yielding benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Staff him with poor scholars of proven integrity and ease their rites so they may counsel frankly.

sentences.zh: 昔魏文帝之在東宮，徐幹、劉楨為友，文學相接之道並如氣類。

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Wendi's being in eastern palace—Xu Gan, Liu Zhen as friends, literary connecting way both like same qi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wendi’s eastern palace had Xu Gan and Liu Zhen as literary friends of like mind.

sentences.zh: 吳太子登，顧譚為友，諸葛恪為賓，臥同床帳，行則參乘，交如布衣，相呼以字，此則近代之明比也。

translations.literal: Wu crown prince Deng—Gu Tan as friend, Zhuge Ke as guest—slept same bed-curtain, in going then three-man carriage, friendship like common cloth, calling each other by style—this is near age's bright comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Wu’s heir Deng shared bed and carriage with Gu Tan and Zhuge Ke like commoners—so should Jin.

sentences.zh: 天子之子不患不富貴，不患人不敬畏，患於驕盈，不聞其過，不知稼穡之艱難耳。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's son does not worry about not being rich honored, not worry about men not revering in awe—worries lie in arrogance filling, not hearing faults, not knowing grain's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: An emperor’s son is already rich—his danger is pride and ignorance of farming.

sentences.zh: 至於甚者，乃不知名六畜，可不勉哉！

translations.literal: Reaching extreme, then not knowing the six livestock's names—can one not exert!
translations.idiomatic: Worst of all he may not know a cow from a horse—train him!

sentences.zh: 昔周公親撻伯禽，曹參笞窋二百，聖考慈父皆不傷恩。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke of Zhou personally flogged Boqin; Cao Shen flogged Kui two hundred—sage father kind father both did not harm grace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Gong flogged his son; Cao Shen beat his—strictness need not break love.

sentences.zh: 今不忍小相維持，令至闕失頓相罪責，不亦誤哉！

translations.literal: Now not bearing small mutual maintenance, letting reach faults then suddenly mutual blame and punishment—is it not error!
translations.idiomatic: Better small correction now than ruin later.

sentences.zh: 在禮太子朝夕視膳，昏定晨省，跪問安否，於情得盡。

translations.literal: In ritual crown prince morning and evening inspects meals, evening settled morning inquired, kneeling asking peace or not—in feeling obtains exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Rites require the heir to attend his parents morning and night.

sentences.zh: 五日一朝，于敬既簡，於恩亦疏，易致構間。

translations.literal: Once every five days one court visit—in respect already summary, in grace also distant, easy to bring frame-ups.
translations.idiomatic: The five-day audience thins filial duty and invites intrigue.

sentences.zh: 故曰「一朝不朝，其間容刀」。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said 'one morning not courted, between it fits a knife.'
translations.idiomatic: The classic warns that even one missed morning lets a knife slip between parent and child.

sentences.zh: 五日之制，起漢高祖，身為天子，父為庶人，萬機事多，故闕私敬耳。

translations.literal: The five-day system arose with Han Gaozu—himself Son of Heaven, father common man—ten thousand threads many affairs—therefore lacked private reverence only.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu invented the five-day rule because he was too busy—our emperor is not.

sentences.zh: 今主上臨朝，太子無事，專主孝養，宜改此俗。

translations.literal: Now lord above faces court, crown prince has no affairs, solely masters filial nurture—ought to change this vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: The heir has time—restore daily filial visits.

sentences.zh: 《文王世子》篇曰：「王季一飯亦一飯，再飯亦再飯。

translations.literal: The 'King Wen's Heir' chapter says: 'Wang Ji one meal also one meal, two meals also two meals.'
translations.idiomatic: The *Book of Rites* says King Wen matched his father meal for meal.

sentences.zh: 」安有逸豫五日一覲哉！

translations.literal: " How can there be ease and five-day audience!
translations.idiomatic: How can a filial son visit only every five days?

sentences.zh: 纘又陳：

translations.literal: Zuan again presented:
translations.idiomatic: He added:

sentences.zh: 今迎太子神柩，孤魂獨行，太孫幼沖，不可涉道。

translations.literal: Now welcoming crown prince's spirit coffin, lone soul walks alone, great-grandson young and tender, cannot tread the road.
translations.idiomatic: The prince’s coffin travels while the great-grandson is too young for the road.

sentences.zh: 謂可遣妃奉迎遠路，令其父衍隨行衛護。

translations.literal: I say one may send consort to welcome on long road, order her father Yan to follow guard.
translations.idiomatic: Send the consort with her father Wei Yan to escort the bier.

sentences.zh: 皇太子初見誣陷，臣家門無祐，三世假親，具嘗辛苦，以家觀國，固知太子有變。

translations.literal: When crown prince first saw slander, your subject's family gate without blessing, three generations borrowed kin, all tasted bitterness—using family to view state, firmly knew crown prince had change.
translations.idiomatic: My low house served the heir through three borrowed postings—I knew the plot early.

sentences.zh: 臣故求副監國，欲依邴吉故事，距違來使，供養擁護，身親飲食醫藥，冀足救危。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore sought deputy overseer of state, wishing according to Bing Ji's precedent, to reject coming envoys, supply nurture and embrace protect, personally attending drink food medicine—hoping enough to save peril.
translations.idiomatic: I begged to be deputy regent like Bing Ji to guard the heir with my own hands.

sentences.zh: 主者以臣名資輕淺，不肯見與。

translations.literal: Presiding officials because your subject's name and credentials were light shallow, would not grant.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucrats refused me as too lowly.

sentences.zh: 世人見笑，謂為此職進退難居，有必死憂。

translations.literal: Worldly men laughed, saying for this office advance-retreat hard to dwell, having certain-death worry.
translations.idiomatic: Men said the post meant certain death.

sentences.zh: 臣獨以為苟全儲君，賈氏所誅，甘心所願。

translations.literal: Your subject alone thought: if only preserving heir-apparent, what Jia clan executed—sweetly willing.
translations.idiomatic: I would die to save the heir—gladly.

sentences.zh: 今監國御史直副皆當三族，侍衛無狀，實自宜然。

translations.literal: Now overseer-of-state censors and deputies all sit three-clans guilt; attendants lacking deportment truly ought to be so.
translations.idiomatic: Regents and guards merit the three-clan law today.

sentences.zh: 臣謂其小人，不足具責。

translations.literal: Your subject calls them petty men—not worth full blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they are small men—punish lightly.

sentences.zh: 故孔子曰：「可以托六尺之孤，臨大節而不可奪。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius said: 'One may entrust him with a six-foot orphan, facing great crisis yet cannot be wrested.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said a tutor must face death for a six-foot orphan.

sentences.zh: 」是以聖王慎選。

translations.literal: " Therefore sage kings choose carefully.
translations.idiomatic: So sage kings choose tutors with care.

sentences.zh: 故河南尹向雄，昔能犯難葬故將鐘會，文帝嘉之，始拔顯用，至於先帝，以為右率。

translations.literal: Therefore former Henan governor Xiang Xiong—formerly could brave difficulty burying former general Zhong Hui—Wendi praised him, first pulled him to prominent use; down to late emperor, made him leader of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong once buried Zhong Hui and rose to right guard—such men should guard the heir.

sentences.zh: 如間之事，若得向雄之比，則豈可觸哉！

translations.literal: If between affairs one obtained Xiang Xiong's sort—then how could they be struck!
translations.idiomatic: Men like Xiang Xiong would not fail.

sentences.zh: 此二使者，但為愚怯，亦非與謀，但可誅身，自全三族。

translations.literal: These two envoys only were foolish cowardly, also not plotting with them—only may execute bodies, self-preserving three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Execute the two foolish envoys alone, spare their kin.

sentences.zh: 如郭俶、郭斌，則于刑為當。

translations.literal: As for Guo Xu, Guo Bin—then in punishment appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xu and Guo Bin deserve full punishment.

sentences.zh: 又東宮亦宜妙選忠直亮正，如向雄比。

translations.literal: Again eastern palace also ought subtly to select loyal straight bright upright, like Xiang Xiong's sort.
translations.idiomatic: Pick guards as loyal as Xiang Xiong for the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 陛下千秋萬歲之後，太孫幼沖，選置兵衛，宜得柱石之士如周昌者。

translations.literal: After Your Majesty's myriad years, great-grandson young and tender—selecting setting arms guard ought to obtain pillar-stone shi like Zhou Chang.
translations.idiomatic: When you die, surround the child with men as staunch as Zhou Chang.

sentences.zh: 世俗淺薄，士無廉節，賈謐小兒，恃寵恣睢，而淺中弱植之徒，更相翕習，故世號魯公二十四友。

translations.literal: Common custom shallow thin, gentlemen without integrity—Jia Mi little boy, relying on favor reckless, while shallow-root weak-plant followers mutually practiced—therefore the age styled Duke Lu's twenty-four friends.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi’s twenty-four ‘friends’ were shallow flatterers.

sentences.zh: 又謐前見臣表理太子，曰：「閻兒作此為健，然觀其意，欲與諸司馬家同。

translations.literal: Again Mi formerly saw your subject's memorial setting right crown prince, said: 'Yan boy does this—being strong; yet observe his intent, wishes with various Sima houses same.'
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi sneered that I sided with the Sima clan.

sentences.zh: 」皆為臣寒心。

translations.literal: " All for your subject chilled the heart.
translations.idiomatic: His words froze my blood.

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書，稱明滿奮、樂廣。

translations.literal: Prostrate I saw edict praising bright Man Fen, Yue Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Your edict praises Man Fen and Yue Guang.

sentences.zh: 侍郎賈胤，與謐親理，而亦疏遠，往免父喪之後，停家五年，雖為小屈，有識貴之。

translations.literal: Attendant Jia Yin—with Mi close in principle, yet also distant—going after exempting father's mourning, stopped home five years—though small bending, those with insight prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yin shunned Jia Mi for five years of mourning—wise men praised him.

sentences.zh: 潘岳、繆征等皆謐父党，共相沈浮，人士羞之，聞其晏然，莫不為怪。

translations.literal: Pan Yue, Miao Zheng and others all Mi's father's party, together sank and floated—gentlemanhood shamed them, hearing they were at peace, none not thought strange.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue and Miao Zheng clung to Jia Mi—honest men despised them.

sentences.zh: 今詔書暴揚其罪，並皆遣出，百姓咸雲清當，臣獨謂非。

translations.literal: Now edict text exposes their crimes, all together sent out—hundred surnames all say pure and right—your subject alone holds it not so.
translations.idiomatic: The court expelled Jia’s circle—people cheer, but I dissent.

sentences.zh: 但嶽征二十四人，宜皆齊黜，以肅風教。

translations.literal: Only Yue Zheng twenty-four men ought all be uniformly dismissed, to purify custom and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Expel Pan Yue’s whole twenty-four, not just a few.

sentences.zh: 朝廷善其忠烈，擢為漢中太守。

translations.literal: The court prized his loyalty and stern integrity, promoted him to prefect of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The court made him prefect of Hanzhong for his blunt loyalty.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫死，既葬，纘以車轢其塚。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao Lun died, already buried, Zuan with cart rolled his tomb mound.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun fell, Yan Zuan drove over his grave.

sentences.zh: 時張華兄子景後徙漢中，纘又表宜還。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Hua's elder brother's son Jing afterward moved to Hanzhong—Zuan again memorialized he ought return.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Zhang Hua’s nephew Zhang Jing to return from Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 纘不護細行，而慷慨好大節。

translations.literal: Zuan did not guard petty conduct, yet was generous and cherished great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan scorned small scruples but loved great honor.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，時年五十九。

translations.literal: He died in office at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 纘五子，皆開朗有才力。

translations.literal: Zuan had five sons—all open bright with talent and strength.
translations.idiomatic: His five sons were all able and open-hearted.

sentences.zh: 長子亨為遼西太守，屬王濬自用其人，亨不得之官。

translations.literal: Eldest son Heng was prefect of Liaoxi—belonging to Wang Jun's using his own men, Heng could not reach office.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yan Heng could not take office in Liaoxi because Wang Jun filled the post himself.

sentences.zh: 依青州刺史苟晞，刑政苛虐，亨數切諫，為晞所害。

translations.literal: He relied on inspector of Qingzhou Gou Xi—punishments and government harsh cruel—Heng several times sharply remonstrated, was harmed by Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Heng served under the harsh Gou Xi and died remonstrating.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷之廢也，天下稱其冤。

translations.literal: The history clerk says: When Minhuai was deposed, all under Heaven called it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Historians say the realm knew Crown Prince Yu was wronged.

sentences.zh: 然皆懼亂政之參夷，懾淫嬖之凶忍，遂使謀臣懷忠而結舌，義士蓄憤而吞聲。

translations.literal: Yet all feared chaotic government's three-clan execution, trembled at wanton favorite's fierce cruelty—thereupon made plotting ministers cherish loyalty yet seal tongues, righteous gentlemen store fury yet swallow voice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet terror of the Jia clan’s cruelty silenced every honest voice.

sentences.zh: 閻續伯官既微于侍郎，位不登於執戟，輕生重義，視死如歸，伏奏而待嚴誅，輿棺以趨鼎鑊，察言觀行，豈非忠直壯乎！

translations.literal: Yan Xubo—office already petty next to attendant, rank not ascending to halberd-bearer—light life heavy righteousness, viewing death as going home, prostrate submitting awaiting stern execution, carrying coffin to hasten cauldron—examining words observing conduct—was he not loyal, straight, and bold!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan, lowlier than a palace attendant, was ready to die in a cauldron for the heir—few courtiers matched even his servants.

sentences.zh: 顧視晉朝公卿，曾不得與其徒隸齒也。

translations.literal: Turning to look at Jin court dukes and ministers—could not even rank with his followers' teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s great lords were less brave than his retainers.

sentences.zh: 茂伯篤終，哭王經以全節。

translations.literal: Maobo finished to the end, weeping Wang Jing to complete integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiong mourned Wang Jing to the end and kept his honor.

sentences.zh: 休然追遠，理鄧艾以成名。

translations.literal: Xiuran traced the distant, setting right Deng Ai to complete a name.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhuo cleared Deng Ai’s name from afar.

sentences.zh: 故得義感明時，仁流枯骨。

translations.literal: Therefore obtained righteousness moving the bright age, benevolence flowing to dry bones.
translations.idiomatic: Their justice moved the age and kindness reached the dead.

sentences.zh: 雖硃勃追論新息，欒布奏事彭王，弗之尚也。

translations.literal: Though Zhu Bo afterward discussed Xinxing, Luan Bu memorialized on Peng king—not surpassing them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bo and Luan Bo did less for the dead than these men.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：感義收會，篤終理艾。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Moved by righteousness burying Hui, finishing to end setting Ai right.
translations.idiomatic: The ode: burying Zhong Hui from duty, clearing Deng Ai from afar.

sentences.zh: 道既相侔，名亦俱泰。

translations.literal: Way already matching each other, name also together great.
translations.idiomatic: Their paths were alike and their fame alike high.

sentences.zh: 續伯區區，輿櫬陳謩。

translations.literal: Xubo tiny, carrying bier stating plans.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan, humble, bore his coffin to counsel the throne.

sentences.zh: 偪茲淫嬖，弗遂良圖。

translations.literal: Pressed by these wanton favorites, good plans not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Wanton favorites blocked his good counsel.

sentences.zh: 啜其泣矣，何嗟及乎！

translations.literal: Sucking their weeping—what sighing reaches!
translations.idiomatic: He wept too late—sighs could not save the day.
